# Buck's packages have to be installed in this order
# devtools::install_github("wStockhausen/wtsQMD")

#  --- Load model results ----
# Ensure rda_ModelsResLst.RData is in the working directory
# written by 03_build_results_object.R
reslst <- wtsUtilities::getObj("Models/rda_ModelsResLst.RData")

# Extract case names
cases <- names(reslst$repsLst)
nCases <- length(cases)

# Create a clean string for referencing models in the text
# Converts "25_1_gmacs" to "25.1.gmacs"
clean_cases <- gsub("_", ".", cases)
strMdls <- ifelse(nCases == 1, "model", "models")

# Build the descriptive string (e.g., "model A, model B, and model C")
if (nCases > 1) {
  strCases <- paste(paste(clean_cases[-nCases], collapse = ", "), 
                    "and", clean_cases[nCases])
} else {
  strCases <- clean_cases
}

# --- Report Configuration ---
# 20% buffer on the OFL: the figure the September 2025 assessment recommended
# and the one historically applied to crab stocks with Tier 3-adequate data. The
# SSC applied 40% for the 2025/26 specification; the divergence is argued in
# Section G.
ABC_buffer     <- 0.8
# Load model definitions. The numbered scripts moved from the repo root into
# scripts/ (2026-08-31 reorganization); accept either location so the document
# knits from both layouts.
source(if (file.exists("0-models.R")) "0-models.R" else "scripts/0-models.R")

# model_defs is now the September set exactly (pruned 2026-08-28), so this is
# normally all of it. It stays as a guard: a model that has not been built yet
# drops out of the tables and the narrative count instead of rendering as a row
# of NAs or zeros. 0-models.R warns by name when that happens. Narrative model
# counts must use n_models, never length(model_defs).
models_present <- model_defs[dir.exists(model_defs)]
n_models       <- length(models_present)

## --- Tier 4: the 2026 harvest specification -------------------------------
## SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the specification scalars. Every downstream
## section (Exec Summary items 5-7, the OFL and ABC sections, status determination,
## Appendix B) must read THESE names and never recompute them -- that is how two
## tables in one document end up disagreeing.
##
## Source is the CSV 07_calc_tier4.R writes. The Phase-1 sketch (§15a) guessed
## at "Models/tier4_results.rds" with a [[VERIFY]] on it; 07 writes a CSV, not an
## RDS, and there is no tier4$by_currency list. Interface is
## currency/Bmsy/B_curr/status/M/Fofl/OFL plus the alternatives.
##
## BASIS (backlog 7d/7e), Grant 2026-08-30, superseding the flat rule decided
## earlier the same day: the RAMPED crab FMP Tier 4 control rule with the BARANOV
## catch equation and a 20% ABC buffer. This is the FMP form and is what the
## October 2025 SSC specified for this stock. The flat rule is retained and
## reported as the sensitivity (OFL_flat). Note the groundfish Tier 5 rule is a
## DIFFERENT tier system and was never a valid citation for a crab stock,
## whichever rule is chosen (2026-08-29;
## the linear F_OFL * B form was the basis before that date). The flat-rule and
## linear-equation alternatives are carried alongside for reporting; neither is
## the basis.
## The September 2025 assessment's Tier 4 OFL on the morphometric currency
## (flat F = M rate, linear catch equation) -- the like-for-like reference for
## this cycle's OFL_flat_linear in Summary of Major Changes item 4. Historical,
## so a literal; the percent change quoted there is computed from it, not typed.
ofl_2025_tier4_morph <- 28.41   # 2025 SAFE, Tier 4 calculation, morphometric

TIER4_CSV <- "data/tier4/tier4_by_currency.csv"
if (file.exists(TIER4_CSV)) {
  tier4_by_currency <- read.csv(TIER4_CSV, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  t4_rec <- tier4_by_currency[tier4_by_currency$currency == "morphometric", ]
  stopifnot("tier4_by_currency.csv has no single morphometric row" = nrow(t4_rec) == 1)
  bmsy_2026        <- t4_rec$Bmsy      # mean REMA-smoothed biomass, years < BMSY_WINDOW_END
  mmb_2026         <- t4_rec$B_curr    # terminal-year REMA-smoothed morphometric MMB
  status_2026      <- t4_rec$status    # mmb_2026 / bmsy_2026
  fofl_2026        <- t4_rec$Fofl
  ofl_2026         <- t4_rec$OFL
  ## Uncertainty on the biomass the control rule uses. Required for Tiers 4-5
  ## by the groundfish guidelines (4.11.2); derivation stated in Section F.
  ## REMA's 95% prediction interval on the SMOOTHED series -- NOT the survey's
  ## own sampling CV, which is an input to that fit.
  mmb_2026_lci     <- t4_rec$B_curr_lci
  mmb_2026_uci     <- t4_rec$B_curr_uci
  mmb_2026_cv      <- t4_rec$B_curr_cv
  ## Status and OFL at the ends of the biomass interval. The OFL bounds are READ
  ## from 07, not derived here. Under the flat rule they could be got by scaling
  ## the point estimate with biomass, because F_OFL was constant; under the ramp
  ## adopted 2026-08-30 F_OFL is itself a function of status, so the OFL is
  ## quadratic in biomass and that shortcut is wrong in both directions -- it
  ## gave [13.82, 24.63] where the correct interval is [10.11, 31.73]. 07 applies
  ## the selected rule and equation at each bound, so this stays right across a
  ## change of either.
  status_2026_lci  <- mmb_2026_lci / bmsy_2026
  status_2026_uci  <- mmb_2026_uci / bmsy_2026
  ofl_2026_lci     <- t4_rec$OFL_lci
  ofl_2026_uci     <- t4_rec$OFL_uci
  stopifnot("OFL interval must bracket the reported OFL" =
              is.na(ofl_2026) || (ofl_2026_lci <= ofl_2026 && ofl_2026 <= ofl_2026_uci))
  ofl_2026_ramp    <- t4_rec$OFL_ramp     # = the reported basis from 2026-08-30
  ## How far the choice of currency moves the OFL, on the SELECTED rule. This was
  ## written as "more than a factor of four" while the flat rule was the basis;
  ## the ramp adopted 2026-08-30 widened it to ~16x, because both large-male
  ## currencies sit just above the beta = 0.25 closure and the ramp cuts their
  ## F_OFL to near zero. Computed, not stated, for that reason.
  ofl_curr_ratio   <- max(tier4_by_currency$OFL) / min(tier4_by_currency$OFL)
  ofl_2026_flat    <- t4_rec$OFL_flat     # sensitivity: flat F_OFL = M, no ramp
  fofl_2026_flat   <- t4_rec$Fofl_flat
  ofl_2026_linear  <- t4_rec$OFL_flat_linear   # flat HCR, linear equation
  ## Sloped rule AND linear equation -- the combination the SSC used to set the
  ## 2025/26 specification, so the like-for-like comparison in Section G.
  ofl_2026_ramp_linear <- t4_rec$OFL_ramp_linear   # reported HCR, linear equation
  NAT_M            <- t4_rec$M            # target F; read, not restated

  ## BMSY_WINDOW_END is a constant inside 07_calc_tier4.R and is not carried in
  ## its output, so the document cannot simply read it. Rather than restate the
  ## literal and let the two drift, recover it: B_MSY is the mean of the REMA
  ## series over years strictly before the cutoff, so the correct cutoff is the
  ## one that reproduces the stored B_MSY. If none does, the constant in 07 has
  ## changed and the document says so instead of printing a stale year.
  ##
  ## The candidate set must run one year PAST the end of the series: with the
  ## full-series window (07's BMSY_WINDOW_END = 2027, i.e. 1982-2026) the cutoff
  ## is not itself a year in the data, and searching only over observed years
  ## silently failed to recover it. What the document actually reports is the
  ## averaging RANGE, not the exclusive cutoff, so build that here.
  BMSY_WINDOW_END <- NA_integer_
  BMSY_WINDOW_LAB <- NA_character_
  if (file.exists("data/tier4/rema_predictions.csv")) {
    .rp <- read.csv("data/tier4/rema_predictions.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    .rp <- .rp[.rp$size == "morphometric", ]
    if (nrow(.rp)) {
      .yrs  <- sort(unique(.rp$Year))
      .cand <- c(.yrs, max(.yrs) + 1L)
      .fit  <- vapply(.cand, function(y) {
        v <- .rp$rema_pred[.rp$Year < y]
        if (!length(v)) NA_real_ else abs(mean(v) - bmsy_2026)
      }, numeric(1))
      if (any(is.finite(.fit)) && min(.fit, na.rm = TRUE) < 1e-6) {
        BMSY_WINDOW_END <- .cand[which.min(.fit)]
        .in <- .yrs[.yrs < BMSY_WINDOW_END]
        BMSY_WINDOW_LAB <- sprintf("%d-%d", min(.in), max(.in))
      }
    }
  }
} else {
  ## Stub so the document still knits before 07 has been run. The empty frame
  ## matters: the Tier 4 and ABC sections select rows out of tier4_by_currency
  ## by currency, and without it those lookups error the knit rather than
  ## printing the not-yet-computed marker.
  tier4_by_currency <- data.frame(
    currency = character(0), Bmsy = numeric(0), B_curr = numeric(0),
    status = numeric(0), Fofl = numeric(0), OFL = numeric(0),
    Fofl_ramp = numeric(0), OFL_ramp = numeric(0), OFL_linear = numeric(0),
    OFL_flat = numeric(0), OFL_ramp_linear = numeric(0),
    M = numeric(0), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  bmsy_2026 <- mmb_2026 <- status_2026 <- fofl_2026 <- ofl_2026 <- NA_real_
  ofl_2026_ramp <- ofl_2026_linear <- ofl_2026_ramp_linear <- NA_real_
  ofl_2026_flat <- fofl_2026_flat <- ofl_curr_ratio <- NA_real_
  mmb_2026_lci <- mmb_2026_uci <- mmb_2026_cv <- NA_real_
  status_2026_lci <- status_2026_uci <- ofl_2026_lci <- ofl_2026_uci <- NA_real_
  NAT_M <- NA_real_
  BMSY_WINDOW_END <- NA_integer_
  BMSY_WINDOW_LAB <- NA_character_
}
## Inline text uses these; render them as a visible marker rather than "NA".
## Length-0 is treated like NA: a currency lookup that matches no row must print
## the marker, not abort the knit on `if (logical(0))`.
.f  <- function(v, d = 3) if (length(v) != 1L || is.na(v)) "[[not yet computed]]" else sprintf(paste0("%.", d, "f"), v)
.fy <- function(v) if (length(v) != 1L || is.na(v)) "[[unrecovered: BMSY_WINDOW_END changed in 07]]" else as.character(v)
# MSST = half the B_MSY proxy, the NPFMC crab FMP definition. The stock is
# overfished if mature male biomass falls below it.
msst_2026 <- 0.5 * bmsy_2026
abc_2026  <- ABC_buffer * ofl_2026    # ABC_buffer <- 0.8, set above

## --- OFL probability distribution (Executive Summary item 8) ----------------
## The OFL is a deterministic function of the terminal smoothed biomass through
## the control rule and the catch equation, so its distribution follows by
## propagating REMA's lognormal prediction interval on that biomass through the
## SAME ramp + Baranov basis 07 applied at the point and at the interval bounds.
## Reconstructed here rather than read because 07 writes no draws file; the
## stopifnot pins the reconstruction to 07's reported OFL and its 95% interval,
## so a change of basis in 07 that this block did not follow aborts the knit
## instead of printing a distribution that disagrees with Section F.
OFL_DRAWS_N <- 200000L
ALPHA_HCR   <- 0.10   # ramp intercept, crab FMP Tier 4 control rule
BETA_HCR    <- 0.25   # closure threshold; OFL = 0 at or below this status
if (!is.na(ofl_2026) && !is.na(mmb_2026) && !is.na(bmsy_2026) &&
    !is.na(mmb_2026_lci) && !is.na(mmb_2026_uci) && mmb_2026 > 0) {
  ## sdlog is REMA's log-scale prediction SD. Take it from the reported CV,
  ## sdlog = sqrt(log(1 + CV^2)) -- the CV is REMA's native uncertainty on the
  ## terminal smoothed biomass, and this does not assume the reported interval is
  ## the exact 95% lognormal one. Cross-check against the interval endpoints,
  ## which must agree because 07 builds the CV and the interval from the same fit.
  .sdlog     <- sqrt(log(1 + mmb_2026_cv^2))
  .sdlog_int <- (log(mmb_2026_uci) - log(mmb_2026_lci)) / (2 * qnorm(0.975))
  stopifnot("REMA CV and 95% interval imply different log-scale SDs" =
              abs(.sdlog - .sdlog_int) < 1e-3)
  set.seed(20260909)
  .b      <- exp(rnorm(OFL_DRAWS_N, log(mmb_2026), .sdlog))
  .status <- .b / bmsy_2026
  .fofl   <- pmin(NAT_M, NAT_M * (.status - ALPHA_HCR) / (1 - ALPHA_HCR))
  .fofl[.status <= BETA_HCR] <- 0
  ofl_draws <- .b * (.fofl / (.fofl + NAT_M)) * (1 - exp(-(.fofl + NAT_M)))
  ofl_draws[.fofl == 0] <- 0
  stopifnot(
    "reconstructed OFL median must match 07's point OFL" =
      abs(stats::median(ofl_draws) - ofl_2026) < 0.25,
    "reconstructed OFL 2.5% must match 07's lower bound" =
      abs(as.numeric(stats::quantile(ofl_draws, 0.025)) - ofl_2026_lci) < 0.5,
    "reconstructed OFL 97.5% must match 07's upper bound" =
      abs(as.numeric(stats::quantile(ofl_draws, 0.975)) - ofl_2026_uci) < 0.5)
} else {
  ofl_draws   <- NULL
}

## --- Observed survey biomass, all three currencies -------------------------
## OBSERVED survey estimates, distinct from the REMA-smoothed B_curr the Tier 4
## calculation uses. Read from data, never hardcoded, so the text cannot drift
## from the survey pull. All in kt.
##   morphometric mature male -> data/derived/survey_indices.csv (the model input)
##   >=95 mm  ("large_male")     -> 02's crabpack pull, BIOMASS_MT
##   >101 mm  ("preferred_male") -> same file
## 2026 is the terminal survey; 2025 is the preceding one, which is what the
## October specification is compared against.
.svy_num <- function(x) if (length(x) == 1L) as.numeric(x) else NA_real_
if (file.exists("data/derived/survey_indices.csv")) {
  .si <- read.csv("data/derived/survey_indices.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  .mm <- .si[.si$sex == "male" & .si$maturity == "mature", ]
  survey_morph_2025 <- .svy_num(.mm$biomass[.mm$year == 2025])
  survey_morph_2026 <- .svy_num(.mm$biomass[.mm$year == 2026])
} else survey_morph_2025 <- survey_morph_2026 <- NA_real_

if (file.exists("data/survey/survey_large_male_index_derived.csv")) {
  .lg <- read.csv("data/survey/survey_large_male_index_derived.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  .get <- function(cat, yr) .svy_num(.lg$BIOMASS_MT[.lg$CATEGORY == cat & .lg$YEAR == yr]) / 1000
  survey_large_2025 <- .get("large_male", 2025);     survey_large_2026 <- .get("large_male", 2026)
  survey_pref_2025  <- .get("preferred_male", 2025); survey_pref_2026  <- .get("preferred_male", 2026)

  ## Preferred males (> 101 mm) are the industry currency and the one the CPT and
  ## the State track, so the terminal estimate is carried in full -- abundance in
  ## millions of crab as well as biomass, both with their survey CVs -- and placed
  ## against the whole 1982- series. Biomass alone understates the case: the
  ## question asked of this stock is how many marketable crab are on the grounds.
  .pref <- .lg[.lg$CATEGORY == "preferred_male", ]
  .pref <- .pref[order(.pref$YEAR), ]
  .pg <- function(col, yr) .svy_num(.pref[[col]][.pref$YEAR == yr])
  pref_abund_2025 <- .pg("ABUNDANCE", 2025) / 1e6      # millions of crab
  pref_abund_2026 <- .pg("ABUNDANCE", 2026) / 1e6
  pref_abund_cv_2026 <- .pg("ABUNDANCE_CV", 2026)
  pref_biom_cv_2026  <- .pg("BIOMASS_MT_CV", 2026)
  pref_biom_chg  <- 100 * (survey_pref_2026 / survey_pref_2025 - 1)
  pref_abund_chg <- 100 * (pref_abund_2026 / pref_abund_2025 - 1)
  pref_n_yrs     <- nrow(.pref)
  pref_rank_2026 <- rank(.pref$BIOMASS_MT)[.pref$YEAR == 2026]   # 1 = lowest on record
  pref_pct_mean  <- 100 * .pref$BIOMASS_MT[.pref$YEAR == 2026] / mean(.pref$BIOMASS_MT)
  stopifnot("preferred-male index must cover both terminal survey years" =
              all(c(2025, 2026) %in% .pref$YEAR))
} else {
  survey_large_2025 <- survey_large_2026 <- survey_pref_2025 <- survey_pref_2026 <- NA_real_
  pref_abund_2025 <- pref_abund_2026 <- pref_abund_cv_2026 <- pref_biom_cv_2026 <- NA_real_
  pref_biom_chg <- pref_abund_chg <- pref_pct_mean <- NA_real_
  pref_n_yrs <- pref_rank_2026 <- NA_integer_
}

## Tier 4 results for ALL THREE currencies, for the comparison table in Section F.
if (exists("tier4_by_currency")) {
  tier4_all <- tier4_by_currency[, intersect(
    ## One-change alternatives to the recommended ramp+Baranov basis: OFL_flat
    ## changes only the control rule; OFL_ramp_linear changes only the equation.
    ## (OFL_ramp is not selected: it equals OFL now that the ramp is the basis.)
    c("currency","Bmsy","B_curr","status","M","Fofl","OFL","OFL_flat","OFL_ramp_linear"),
    names(tier4_by_currency))]
} else tier4_all <- NULL

# Case selection
# SEPTEMBER 2026 PORT — repointed from the May candidate bracket to the accepted model.
# Accepted (RECOMMENDED) model = "26.1 gmacs (update + compfix + plus group + new_mat)"
# (Models/26_gmacs_update_newmat_plus_group, shortname Model 26.1b) -- May's 25.2c advanced to
# end year 2025, i.e. fishery through 2025 and survey through 2026. Repointed 2026-08-28; it
# previously named the *May* folder (terminal 2024), which would have reported the wrong fit.
# Reference (2025 accepted, rolled forward) = "25.1 gmacs" (Models/25_gmacs).
# These names must match the case names produced when rda_ModelsResLst.RData is regenerated (03_build_results_object.R).
# >>> REVIEW: confirm comparison pairs once the 2026 results object exists.
accepted_model      <- "26.1 gmacs (update + compfix + plus group + new_mat)"
reference_model     <- "25.1 gmacs"
case_for_resids     <- accepted_model                            # model to print size-comp residuals for
case_for_data_table <- c(reference_model, accepted_model)
case_for_mat_plot   <- c(reference_model, accepted_model)        # show effect of new maturity (reference lacks new_mat)
report_model <- model_defs[accepted_model]

## --- Tier 3 quantities for the author-recommended model ---------------------
## Read once, here, so the Executive Summary can contrast the Tier 3 answer with
## the Tier 4 one without either being retyped. Same source the step-change table
## reads (Table \@ref(tab:stepchange)); nothing is recomputed.
.t3 <- local({
  f <- file.path(report_model, "Gmacsall.out")
  out <- list(bmsy = NA_real_, status = NA_real_, ofl = NA_real_,
              mmb = NA_real_, mmb_proj = NA_real_, year = NA_real_)
  if (!file.exists(f)) return(out)
  tmp <- readLines(f, warn = FALSE)
  grab <- function(key) {
    l <- grep(paste0("^", key, " :"), tmp, value = TRUE)[1]
    if (is.na(l)) NA_real_ else as.numeric(strsplit(trimws(l), " +")[[1]][3])
  }
  out$bmsy   <- grab("BMSY")
  out$status <- grab("Bcurr/BMSY")
  out$ofl    <- grab("OFL\\(tot\\)")
  ## GMACS's status is Bcurr/BMSY, in which Bcurr is the PROJECTED mature male
  ## biomass the control rule acts on -- not the terminal MMB at mating read
  ## from the Summary block below. Carrying only one of the two invited exactly
  ## the error this fixes: the Executive Summary paired terminal MMB of 141.5 kt
  ## with a status of 1.32 and told the reader 141.5 was above a proxy of 145.0
  ## (2026-08-29). Both are kept, and each is named where it is used.
  out$mmb_proj <- if (is.na(out$status) || is.na(out$bmsy)) NA_real_ else
                    out$status * out$bmsy
  s <- grep("^Summary: dataframe", tmp)[1]
  if (!is.na(s)) {
    rows <- character(0)
    for (ln in tmp[(s + 2):length(tmp)]) {
      if (!nzchar(trimws(ln)) || startsWith(ln, ">")) break
      rows <- c(rows, ln)
    }
    if (length(rows)) {
      last <- strsplit(trimws(tail(rows, 1)), " +")[[1]]
      out$year <- as.numeric(last[1]); out$mmb <- as.numeric(last[2])
    }
  }
  out
})


# Global Switches
do_size_comps  <- 1 # Set to 1 to regenerate PNGs (can take time)
do_proj        <- 0 # Set to 1 to process projection files
make_proj_fig  <- 0 # Set to 1 to generate projection plots

# --- Plot size comp ----
if(do_size_comps==1){
  # Extract results using Buck's package tools
  dfrZCs <- wtsGMACS::extractRep1Results(reslst, "Size_fit_summary") |> 
    dplyr::mutate(across(c(year, size, inpSS, inpN, aggObs, aggPrd, aggRes), as.numeric))
  
  # 2. Assign models to Groups
  # Maturity ogive and hybrid status will affect
  dfrZCs <- dfrZCs |> 
    dplyr::mutate(
      fleet = dplyr::case_when(
        grepl("compfix", case, ignore.case = TRUE) & fleet == "Pot_Fishery" ~ "Pot_fishery_compfix",
        grepl("hyb_surv|hyb_both", case, ignore.case = TRUE) & fleet == "NMFS_Trawl_1982" ~ "NMFS_Trawl_1982_hybrid",
        grepl("hyb_surv|hyb_both", case, ignore.case = TRUE) & fleet == "NMFS_Trawl_1989" ~ "NMFS_Trawl_1989_hybrid",
        .default = fleet
      ),
      fleet = ifelse(
        grepl("plus group", case, ignore.case = TRUE) & fleet == "Pot_Fishery", "Pot_fishery_plus_group", fleet),
      fleet = ifelse(
        grepl("hyb_fishery|hyb_both", case, ignore.case = TRUE) & fleet == "Pot_Fishery", "Pot_fishery_hybrid", fleet),
    maturity_ogive = ifelse(grepl("new_mat", case, ignore.case = TRUE), 
                           "New maturity", 
                           "Old maturity"),
    ) |>
    dplyr::group_by(fleet, maturity_ogive, comp_type, sex, maturity) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(comp_id = dplyr::cur_group_id())
  
  # Plotting Logic
  unique_comps <- dfrZCs |> distinct(comp_id, aggID, fleet, comp_type, sex, maturity_ogive, maturity, shell_cond, case) # Grant: case, may not be needed...
  
  for (i in seq_along(unique(unique_comps$comp_id))) { # Loop around comp data types
    curr_id <- i
    tmp     <- dfrZCs |> filter(comp_id == curr_id)
    
    # Size Composition Plot (use shortnames in the legend)
    tmp$case_short <- to_short(tmp$case)
    p <- ggplot(tmp) +
      geom_bar(aes(x = as.numeric(size), y = aggObs), stat = "identity", position = "identity", fill = 'lightgrey') +
      geom_line(aes(x = as.numeric(size), y = aggPrd, col = case_short)) +
      facet_wrap(~year) +
      theme_bw() +
      labs(x = "Carapace width (mm)", y = "Proportion", col = "Model",
           title = paste(tmp$fleet[1], tmp$sex[1], tmp$comp_type[1], tmp$maturity[1], tmp$maturity_ogive[1],  sep = " / "))
    
    compname <- paste(tmp$fleet[1], tmp$sex[1], tmp$comp_type[1], tmp$maturity[1], tmp$maturity_ogive[1], sep = "_")
    ggsave(paste0("plots/size_comp_plot_",  curr_id, "_", compname, ".png"), p, height = 8, width = 8, dpi = 300)
    
    # Residual Plot for specific case
    res_data <- tmp |> 
      filter(case == case_for_resids) |> 
      mutate(raw_res = aggObs - aggPrd)
    
    p_res <- ggplot(res_data) +
      geom_point(aes(x = year, y = size, size = abs(raw_res), col = as.factor(sign(raw_res))), alpha = 0.9) +
      theme_bw() +
      labs(x = "Year", y = "Carapace width (mm)", col = "Residual direction", size = "Raw residual size")
    
    ggsave(paste0("plots/size_comp_resid_", curr_id, "_", compname, ".png"), p_res, height = 10, width = 8, dpi = 300)
  }
}




#=================================
# this code pulls the projections for selected models
# to do the projections, follow these steps:
# this requires a converged model with a hessian
# make a new folder with the model to project in it, specify projection details in .PROJ file
# .PROJ file needs to change strategies
# save .par file as .pin file
# run '.\gmacs.exe -phase 6 -nohess -mcmc 1 -mcsave 1'
# that executes one draw (at the MLE) of MCMC and saves the results
# run '.\gmacs.exe -mceval -noest' in that folder to write output to 'mcoutPROJ.REP'
# run code below to pull relevant info, be sure to modify years to make 'mcoutPROJ.REP'

# BE SURE TO CHANGE THE F IN THE PROJ FILE TO THE FOFL
proj_dir <- file.path(getwd(), report_model)

if(do_proj==1)
{
  proj_dirs<-c(paste(proj_dir,"proj/mcoutPROJSSB.REP",sep=''))
  
  proj_mmb_under_ofl<-rep(NA,length(proj_dirs))
  proj_stat_ofl<-rep(NA,length(proj_dirs))
  proj_mmb_under_nof<-rep(NA,length(proj_dirs))
  proj_stat_nof<-rep(NA,length(proj_dirs))
  
  for(x in 1:length(proj_dirs))
  {
    innames<-c("Draw","Replicate","Treatment",paste("F",seq(1,4)),
               "B35",seq(1982,2035))
    projfile<-as.data.frame(matrix(scan(proj_dirs[x],skip=1),ncol=length(innames),byrow=TRUE))
    colnames(projfile)<-innames
    
    proj_mmb_under_ofl[x]<-filter(projfile,Treatment==2)$'2025'[1]
    proj_stat_ofl[x]<-proj_mmb_under_ofl[x]/filter(projfile,Treatment==2)$'B35'[1]
    
    proj_mmb_under_nof[x]<-filter(projfile,Treatment==1)$'2025'[1]
    proj_stat_nof[x]<- proj_mmb_under_nof[x]/filter(projfile,Treatment==2)$'B35'[1]
  }
}


if(make_proj_fig==1)
{
  #==make a figure that shows projections under given assumptions about rec and M and F
  yams<-melt(projfile[,c(1,2,3,4,9:ncol(projfile))],id.vars=c("Draw","Replicate","Treatment","F 1"))
  yams$Treatment<-c("No fishing","OFL")[yams$Treatment]
  meds<-yams%>%
    group_by(Treatment,variable)%>%
    summarize(med_ssb=median(value))
  
  #==compare to survey biomass
  tmp<-readLines(paste(report_model,"/Gmacsall.out",sep=''))   # was model_defs[1] (reference); use the accepted report model, which is guaranteed run
  male_wt_len<-as.numeric(filter(reslst$repsLst[[names(report_model)]]$IndivWeightByXM,Sex=="male"&Year=="1982"&Maturity=='mature')[,4:25])
  
  #==mature males
  st<-grep(c("N(males): dataframe"),tmp,fixed=TRUE)
  tmp2<-tmp[st:(st+50)]
  tmp3<-tmp2[grep("1982",tmp2)[1]:(grep("EOD",tmp2)-1)]
  
  N_males<-NULL
  for(x in 1:length(tmp3))
    N_males<-rbind(N_males,as.numeric(unlist(strsplit(tmp3[x],split=" "))))
  
  
  sweep1<-sweep(N_males[,3:ncol(N_males)],2,male_wt_len,FUN='*')
  sizes<-seq(27.5,132.5,5)
  mat_95<-rep(0,length(sizes))
  mat_95[sizes>95]<-1  
  mat_95[sizes<95&sizes>90]<-0.5
  sweep2<-apply(sweep(sweep1,2,mat_95,FUN='*'),1,sum)/1000000
  surv_lg_male<-data.frame(Year=N_males[,1],MMB=sweep2)
  
  png(paste("plots/projections.png",sep=""),height=8,width=8,res=300,units='in')
  ggplot()+
    geom_line(data=yams,aes(x=as.numeric(as.character(variable)),y=value,col=as.factor(Treatment),group=interaction(Replicate,Treatment)),alpha=.3)+
    geom_line(data=meds,aes(x=as.numeric(as.character(variable)),y=med_ssb,col=as.factor(Treatment)),lwd=2)+
    geom_line(data=filter(meds,as.numeric(as.character(variable))<2026),aes(x=as.numeric(as.character(variable)),y=med_ssb,col=as.factor(Treatment)),lwd=2,col='grey')+
    theme_bw()+ylab("MMB (>=95mm)")+
    xlab("Year")+labs(color="Fishing")+ylim(0,900)+
    geom_line(data=surv_lg_male,aes(x=Year,y=MMB))
  dev.off()
}

<!-- The jitter scalars are loaded here, ahead of the Executive Summary, because
     the summary quotes the recovery rate of the accepted fit. Section E is where
     they are discussed. This chunk only defines them. -->

```{r jitter-setup, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# Jitter outputs, written by 05_run_jitter.R. Every jitter value quoted in this
# document is pulled from this object at knit time so the text cannot drift
# from the runs. Absent runs yield NA and a visible note, never a plausible
# placeholder.
jit_path <- "Models/rda_jitter.RData"
jit_have <- file.exists(jit_path)
if (jit_have) load(jit_path)          # -> `jitter`: results / summary / modes / attribution / manifest

## 05_run_jitter.R writes this path for WHATEVER model it was given, so a jitter
## on any other configuration silently leaves its results here. On 2026-08-30 this
## file held 26_gmacs_combined for a period; a render then would have relabelled
## that model's diagnostics as the accepted model's, in the section the SSC asked
## for, with nothing on the page looking wrong. Assert the identity instead --
## this guard CAN fire on the case it exists to protect, unlike a check against a
## baseline that has been deleted.
if (jit_have) stopifnot(
  "Models/rda_jitter.RData is not the accepted model -- another model's jitter overwrote it" =
    identical(as.character(jitter$summary$model[1]), "26_gmacs_update_newmat_plus_group"))

jit_sum <- if (jit_have) jitter$summary   else NULL
jit_res <- if (jit_have) jitter$results   else NULL
jit_man <- if (jit_have) jitter$manifest  else NULL

.js <- function(field, default = NA) {          # NA-safe accessor on the summary row
  if (!jit_have || !field %in% names(jit_sum)) return(default)
  jit_sum[[field]][1]
}
jit_fmt <- function(x, d = 2) if (is.null(x) || length(x) == 0 || is.na(x)) "NA" else
  formatC(x, format = "f", digits = d, big.mark = "")

## Male-only's recovery of ITS OWN BEST fit, on the same convention used for the
## accepted model and in Appendix C: runs within 0.01 nll of that model's minimum,
## over converged runs. NOT the rate against `base_nll` -- that model was promoted,
## so its base is a superseded fit and scoring against it gives 12.0% where the
## accepted fit is recovered 25.3% of the time (found by review, 2026-08-30).
.mo_path <- "Models/rda_jitter_male_only.RData"
if (file.exists(.mo_path)) {
  .mo <- new.env(); load(.mo_path, envir = .mo)
  .mor <- .mo$jitter$results
  .mok <- !is.na(.mor$mode)
  .mobest <- min(.mor$objFun[.mok], na.rm = TRUE)
  jit_mo_pct <- 100 * sum(abs(.mor$objFun[.mok] - .mobest) < 0.01) / sum(.mok)
  stopifnot("male-only jitter file is not the male-only model" =
              identical(as.character(.mo$jitter$summary$model[1]), "26_gmacs_male_only"))
} else jit_mo_pct <- NA_real_

jit_n         <- .js("n_runs")
jit_sd        <- .js("jitter_sd")
jit_conv      <- .js("n_converged")
jit_complete  <- .js("n_complete")
jit_pct_best  <- .js("pct_at_best_mode")
jit_base_nll  <- .js("base_nll")
jit_best_nll  <- .js("best_nll")
jit_improve   <- .js("nll_improvement")
jit_ofl_min   <- .js("ofl_min");  jit_ofl_max <- .js("ofl_max")
jit_mmb_min   <- .js("mmb_min");  jit_mmb_max <- .js("mmb_max")
jit_term_yr   <- .js("terminal_year")
jit_promoted  <- isTRUE(.js("promoted", FALSE))

# Number of distinct optima the runs settled into ("minor" = clusters too small
# to count as a mode, see classify_modes() in R/gmacs_jitter.R).
jit_nmodes <- if (jit_have)
  length(setdiff(unique(jit_res$mode[!is.na(jit_res$mode)]), "minor")) else NA_integer_
jit_multimodal <- !is.na(jit_nmodes) && jit_nmodes > 1

## How many runs actually recover the fit this document reports?
##
## `pct_at_best_mode` is NOT that number. classify_modes() (R/gmacs_jitter.R)
## letters a cluster only once at least three runs share it, so a solution found
## by one or two runs is bucketed as "minor" -- and for the recommended model the
## accepted fit IS such a solution. Its nll, -23546.3458, is the best any run
## reached, while lettered mode A is 0.81 units worse and holds the 5.1 percent
## the statistic reports. Describing that as "the best-fitting mode" inverted the
## diagnostic (found 2026-08-29); the honest figure is worse, not better.
jit_n_conv    <- if (jit_have) sum(!is.na(jit_res$mode)) else NA_integer_
jit_n_at_base <- if (jit_have)
  sum(abs(jit_res$objFun[!is.na(jit_res$mode)] - jit_base_nll) < 0.01) else NA_integer_
jit_pct_at_base <- if (jit_have && !is.na(jit_n_conv) && jit_n_conv > 0)
  100 * jit_n_at_base / jit_n_conv else NA_real_
## The reported fit must be at least as good as every lettered mode, or the
## document is reporting something other than the best solution found.
if (jit_have) stopifnot(
  "a lettered jitter mode beats the reported fit" =
    jit_base_nll <= min(jit_res$objFun[!is.na(jit_res$mode) & jit_res$mode != "minor"]) + 1e-6)
```

# Executive Summary

This is the September 2026 stock assessment for eastern Bering Sea (EBS) snow crab (*Chionoecetes opilio*), prepared for the Crab Plan Team and the Scientific and Statistical Committee, and provides the basis for the 2026/27 harvest specifications.

The stock was declared overfished in October 2021 and is rebuilding under Amendment 53. The directed fishery was closed for the 2022 and 2023 seasons and has since reopened at a reduced scale. The State set a total allowable catch of 4.22 kt for 2025/26, of which 4.13 kt was retained.

Stock status is reported under a Tier 4 assessment rather than from the Tier 3 size-structured model. The Tier 4 assessment is a random-effects (REMA) model fit to the NMFS summer survey morphometrically mature male biomass series. This follows the October 2025 and June 2026 SSC recommendations that Tier 4 be used until the Tier 3 model's convergence problems are resolved.

Morphometrically mature male biomass (males with a large claw relative to their carapace width, the definition of maturity used for management of this stock) from the Tier 4 stock assessment is estimated to be `r .f(mmb_2026, 1)` kt in 2026, which is `r .f(100*status_2026, 0)` percent of the B~MSY~ proxy of `r .f(bmsy_2026, 1)` kt and above the minimum stock size threshold of `r .f(msst_2026, 1)` kt. Under this definition of mature male biomass, the stock is not overfished. The 95 percent confidence interval ranges from `r .f(mmb_2026_lci, 1)` to `r .f(mmb_2026_uci, 1)` kt. That interval is above the minimum stock size threshold and includes the B~MSY~ proxy, so a rebuilt stock cannot be ruled out. However, given the width of that interval and the uncertainty in whether morphometric maturity reflects the reproductive potential of the stock, the authors do not consider the stock rebuilt.

The Tier 3 model (Model 26.1b, the author-preferred configuration) is more optimistic. It estimates mature male biomass at mating of `r .f(.t3$mmb, 1)` kt in `r .f(.t3$year, 0)`, the model's terminal year, and projects `r .f(.t3$mmb_proj, 1)` kt for February `r .f(.t3$year + 1, 0)`, when the control rule is applied. This corresponds to a status of `r .f(.t3$status, 2)`, above its B~MSY~ proxy of `r .f(.t3$bmsy, 1)` kt.

However, the Tier 3 model does not converge to a single solution. Jittering the starting values produced several minima with similar likelihoods but substantially different management quantities. Therefore, the Tier 3 OFL is deemed unreliable and the authors recommend the Tier 4 model. Tier 3 results are reported in Section E.

Following the June 2026 SSC recommendation, the overfishing limit is calculated under Tier 4 using morphometrically mature male biomass until a more stable Tier 3 model can be developed. Based on the Tier 4 harvest control rule, the OFL is `r .f(ofl_2026, 2)` kt, and the ABC after a `r sprintf("%.0f", 100*(1-ABC_buffer))` percent buffer is `r .f(abc_2026, 2)` kt (the basis for the buffer is described in Section G). For scale, the OFL exceeds the observed biomass of commercially preferred males (>101 mm) in the 2026 survey, `r .f(survey_pref_2026, 1)` kt.

## Management performance {-}

```{r mgmt-performance, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
## Executive Summary item 6. The checklist requires the last five crab years of
## MMB, OFL, MSST, ABC, TAC and retained catch, in BOTH 1,000 t and million lb.
##
## BASIS (Grant, 2026-08-29): the values AS SPECIFIED at the time, not restated
## from this cycle's model. The checklist is explicit -- "the record of specified
## management reference points are not updated in those tables since they were
## the basis for SSC and Council decision-making" -- and the September 2025
## assessment used the same convention (its Tier 3 and >= 95 mm tables carry
## identical rows for every year before the terminal one).
##
## The consequence is visible and is footnoted below the table: MMB falls from
## 106.52 to 60.08 kt between 2023/24 and 2024/25 because the SSC determined
## that year's status on the TIER 4 assessment, not because the stock fell. Every
## row is sourced in data/historical/management_performance.csv.
# 1,000 t -> million lb, the second rendering the checklist requires.
MLB_PER_KT <- 2.20462262

mp_path <- "data/historical/management_performance.csv"
mp_have <- file.exists(mp_path)
if (mp_have) {
  mp <- read.csv(mp_path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE)
  stopifnot("management_performance.csv must carry five crab years" = nrow(mp) == 5L)

  .mp_cols <- c(msst = "MSST", mmb = "MMB", tac = "TAC", retained = "Retained catch",
                total_catch = "Total catch", ofl = "OFL", abc = "ABC")

  ## Tier of the MMB and MSST values in each row, derived from the CSV's
  ## mmb_basis column (Tier 3 status determinations for 2021/22-2023/24;
  ## Tier 4 for 2024/25 and 2025/26). Column requested by GA review 2026-08-31.
  mp_table <- function(scale, unit_label, digits) {
    d <- data.frame(Year = mp$crab_year,
                    Tier = ifelse(grepl("^Tier 4", mp$mmb_basis), "4", "3"),
                    check.names = FALSE)
    for (nm in names(.mp_cols)) d[[.mp_cols[[nm]]]] <- mp[[nm]] * scale
    flextable::flextable(d) |>
      flextable::fontsize(size = 9, part = "all") |>
      flextable::colformat_double(j = unname(.mp_cols), digits = digits) |>
      flextable::autofit() |>
      flextable::set_caption(
        caption = paste0(
          "Management performance across the five most recent assessments (", unit_label,
          "). Values are those used to set the specifications in each year, ",
          "not values re-estimated by the current assessment."),
        autonum = officer::run_autonum(seq_id = "tab", pre_label = "Table ",
                                       bkm = paste0("mgmt-performance-", gsub("[^a-z]", "", tolower(unit_label))))
      )
  }
}
```

```

\Needspace{12\baselineskip}

```{r mgmt-performance-lb, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}

```

The table reports the values used to set the harvest specifications in each year, not values re-estimated by the current assessment. Mature male biomass (MMB) and the minimum stock size threshold (MSST) come from two different tiers: Tier 3 estimates for 2021/22 to 2023/24 and Tier 4 estimates for 2024/25 and 2025/26, as accepted by the SSC in each year. The status determination for a crab year is made the following October, after that year's survey, and can use a different tier from the specification made the year before: the 2024/25 OFL and ABC were specified in October 2024 under Tier 3 (Table \@ref(tab:basis-ofl)), while the 2024/25 status determination was made in October 2025 using the Tier 4 assessment, and it is the determination values that are shown here. The drop in MMB from `r if (mp_have) .f(mp$mmb[mp$crab_year == "2023/24"], 2) else "NA"` to `r if (mp_have) .f(mp$mmb[mp$crab_year == "2024/25"], 2) else "NA"` kt reflects the change in tier. The subsequent increase to `r if (mp_have) .f(mp$mmb[mp$crab_year == "2025/26"], 2) else "NA"` kt for 2025/26 occurred within Tier 4 and reflects an increase in the smoothed observed survey biomass. The 2025/26 total allowable catch included a 1 million lb hybrid add-on. Two estimates of 2025/26 mature male biomass appear here: the `r if (mp_have) .f(mp$mmb[mp$crab_year == "2025/26"], 2) else "NA"` kt in the table is the estimate from the September 2025 assessment that was used to set the 2025/26 specification, and the `r .f(mmb_2026, 2)` kt in Table \@ref(tab:current-status) is the updated estimate for the same crab year from this assessment, which includes the 2026 survey. The minimum stock size threshold shown for 2024/25 and 2025/26, `r if (mp_have) .f(mp$msst[mp$crab_year == "2025/26"], 2) else "NA"` kt, is likewise the value specified in October 2025. This assessment's updated threshold is `r .f(msst_2026, 2)` kt (Table \@ref(tab:current-status)).

The stock was determined to be overfished for 2024/25, when mature male biomass of `r if (mp_have) .f(mp$mmb[mp$crab_year == "2024/25"], 2) else "NA"` kt was below the minimum stock size threshold of `r if (mp_have) .f(mp$msst[mp$crab_year == "2024/25"], 2) else "NA"` kt, and it remains in the rebuilding plan. Overfishing did not occur in any of the five years shown: total catch was below the specified OFL.

## Current status of the stock {-}

```{r current-status, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
## Executive Summary "Current Status" table -- SSC Table 1, the new Table 3 the
## May 2026 CPT describes. Column set follows the SSC's own: tier, MSST, B_MSY,
## MMB for the just-completed crab year, MMB/B_MSY, that year's OFL, its total
## catch, and rebuilding status.
##
## The CPT's rule pairs reference points from TWO assessments on purpose: MSST
## from the most recent (this one) and B_MSY from the previous. The B_MSY
## carried here is therefore the 142.79 kt the SSC specified for 2025/26, not
## this cycle's 146.56 kt.
##
## MMB is where the Tier 4 basis and the required column do not meet, and the
## table is footnoted for it rather than fudged: the CPT asks for mature male
## biomass in February after fishing, and Tier 4 produces a REMA-smoothed
## SURVEY biomass, which is neither projected forward nor at the time of mating.
## The SSC footnotes its own table the same way.
cs_bmsy_prev <- 142.79     # October 2025 SSC report, Table 2 (2025/26 specification)
cs_ofl_prev  <- 20.11      # OFL specified for the just-completed crab year, same source

cs_df <- data.frame(
  `Crab year`   = "2025/26",
  MSST          = msst_2026,
  `B_MSY`       = cs_bmsy_prev,
  MMB           = mmb_2026,
  `MMB/B_MSY`   = mmb_2026 / cs_bmsy_prev,
  OFL           = cs_ofl_prev,
  `Total catch` = 7.10,
  `Rebuilding status` = "rebuilding",
  check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

flextable::flextable(cs_df) |>
  # 9 columns measured 7.12 in against the 6.5 in portrait line; this table sits
  # in the Executive Summary and must not be turned landscape (2026-08-29).
  flextable::fontsize(size = 8, part = "all") |>
  flextable::colformat_double(j = c("MSST","B_MSY","MMB","OFL","Total catch"), digits = 2) |>
  flextable::colformat_double(j = "MMB/B_MSY", digits = 3) |>
  flextable::autofit() |>
  flextable::set_caption(
    caption = paste(
      "Current status of the eastern Bering Sea snow crab stock under Tier 4",
      "(biomass, OFL and catch in 1,000 t). MSST is from this assessment. The B_MSY proxy is the one",
      "specified for 2025/26 in the October 2025 SSC report, following the May 2026",
      "CPT convention that the two come from different assessment years. Mature",
      "male biomass is the Tier 4 estimate at the time of the survey, not at the",
      "time of mating and not projected forward after fishing. See the note below.",
      "OFL and total catch are for the completed 2025/26 crab year."),
    autonum = officer::run_autonum(seq_id = "tab", pre_label = "Table ", bkm = "current-status")
  )
```

**Is the stock subject to overfishing?** No. Total catch in 2025/26 was 7.10 kt compared to the OFL of 20.11 kt.

**Is the stock overfished?** No. Mature male biomass of `r .f(mmb_2026, 2)` kt is above the minimum stock size threshold of `r .f(msst_2026, 2)` kt, and the 95 percent confidence interval remains above the MSST (Section F). The stock was determined to be overfished for 2024/25 and remains in the rebuilding plan adopted under Amendment 53. It has not yet reached the biomass at which it would be declared rebuilt, the B~MSY~ proxy of `r .f(bmsy_2026, 1)` kt (Section H).

**Is the stock approaching an overfished condition?** Unknown. Answering this question requires a reliable projection of mature male biomass. The Tier 3 models do not converge reliably and their recruitment estimates have high retrospective bias, and the Tier 4 assessment produces no projection, so no reliable projection is available.

Under Tier 4, biomass is taken from the REMA smooth of the NMFS summer survey, so the value is an estimate at the time of the survey. It is not mature male biomass in February after fishing, which is what a Tier 3 model supplies from its projection. The two are not interchangeable, and no projection to the time of mating is made here. The October 2025 SSC report notes the same substitution, footnoting that "snow crab MMB represents an estimate at the time of the survey, not at the time of mating".

## Basis for the OFL {-}

\Needspace{14\baselineskip}

```{r basis-ofl, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
## Executive Summary item 7. Year, tier and subtier, M, B_MSY and the years it
## averages over, projected MMB, MMB/B_MSY and F_OFL, for the last five crab
## years -- the fields the checklist asks for, in the order the SSC's own
## specification table uses.
##
## Rows for 2022/23 to 2025/26 are the SPECIFIED values, read from the Table 2
## of each October SSC report, matching the basis used for management
## performance above. The 2026/27 row is this assessment and is filled at knit
## time from the Tier 4 scalars, so it cannot drift from Section F.
bo_path <- "data/historical/basis_for_ofl.csv"
bo_have <- file.exists(bo_path)
if (bo_have) {
  bo <- read.csv(bo_path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE)
  stopifnot("basis_for_ofl.csv must carry five crab years" = nrow(bo) == 5L,
            "the last row must be this cycle" = bo$crab_year[nrow(bo)] == "2026/27")

  ## Fill the current row from the Tier 4 calculation rather than restating it.
  .i <- nrow(bo)
  bo$m[.i]          <- NAT_M
  bo$bmsy[.i]       <- bmsy_2026
  bo$bmsy_basis[.i] <- if (is.na(BMSY_WINDOW_LAB)) "NA" else BMSY_WINDOW_LAB
  bo$proj_mmb[.i]   <- mmb_2026
  bo$status[.i]     <- status_2026
  bo$fofl[.i]       <- fofl_2026
  bo$ofl[.i]        <- ofl_2026
  stopifnot("2026/27 row did not fill from the Tier 4 scalars" =
              !is.na(bo$ofl[.i]) && !is.na(bo$bmsy[.i]))

  bo_df <- data.frame(
    `Crab year`     = bo$crab_year,
    Tier            = bo$tier,
    M               = as.numeric(bo$m),
    `B_MSY`         = as.numeric(bo$bmsy),
    `B_MSY basis`   = bo$bmsy_basis,
    `Projected MMB` = as.numeric(bo$proj_mmb),
    `MMB/B_MSY`     = as.numeric(bo$status),
    `F_OFL`         = as.numeric(bo$fofl),
    OFL             = as.numeric(bo$ofl),
    check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

  flextable::flextable(bo_df) |>
    flextable::fontsize(size = 7, part = "all") |>   # 9pt measured 7.05 in and 8pt 6.56 in, both over the 6.5 in line
    flextable::colformat_double(j = c("M", "F_OFL"), digits = 2) |>
    flextable::colformat_double(j = c("B_MSY", "Projected MMB", "OFL"), digits = 2) |>
    flextable::colformat_double(j = "MMB/B_MSY", digits = 3) |>
    flextable::autofit() |>
    flextable::set_caption(
      caption = paste(
        "Basis for the OFL over the five most recent crab years (biomass and OFL",
        "in 1,000 t; M per year). Values for 2022/23 to 2025/26 are those used",
        "to set the specifications in each year. The 2026/27 row is the Tier 4",
        "model recommended in this document."),
      autonum = officer::run_autonum(seq_id = "tab", pre_label = "Table ", bkm = "basis-ofl")
    )
}
```

`r if (!bo_have) "*Basis-for-the-OFL table not available: data/historical/basis_for_ofl.csv is missing.*"`

The stock moved from Tier 3 to Tier 4 for the 2025/26 specification because the October 2025 SSC found the Tier 3 model's convergence problems severe enough to prevent its use for advice. The 2026/27 recommendation continues with the Tier 4 assessment given continued convergence problems with the Tier 3 model. The values for 2022/23 to 2025/26 are the values the SSC specified in each year, taken from Table 2 of the corresponding October SSC report (i.e. they are not re-estimated here). The 2026/27 row is from the Tier 4 model in this assessment. The change of tier affects the table in three ways. First, the B~MSY~ proxy under Tier 4 is the mean of the smoothed survey time series rather than a spawning-biomass-per-recruit reference point, so both its value and its averaging period change between 2024/25 and 2025/26. Second, F~OFL~ under Tier 4 is set by the sloped control rule at each year's stock status, so it is below M whenever status is below one. This applies to the 0.19 specified for 2025/26 and to the 2026/27 row. The Tier 3 F~OFL~ values are on the scale used in the source tables and are not comparable with M or with the Tier 4 values. Third, mature male biomass for the Tier 4 years is an estimate at the time of the survey, not at mating, and is the terminal smoothed value, not a projection (October 2025 SSC report).

## OFL probability distribution {-}

The OFL depends on the terminal smoothed survey biomass through the control rule and the catch equation. The REMA model assumes that biomass follows a lognormal distribution. The terminal biomass has a mean of `r .f(mmb_2026, 1)` kt and a coefficient of variation of `r .f(100*mmb_2026_cv, 1)` percent. Propagating that distribution through the sloped control rule and the Baranov catch equation gives the distribution in Figure \@ref(fig:ofl-distribution). The median is `r .f(ofl_2026, 2)` kt and the 95 percent confidence interval ranges from `r .f(ofl_2026_lci, 2)` to `r .f(ofl_2026_uci, 2)` kt. The distribution has a kink in its upper tail where biomass reaches the B~MSY~ proxy. Below the proxy, F~OFL~ rises along the ramp as biomass rises, so the OFL grows through both terms. Above the proxy the rule caps F~OFL~ at M, the OFL grows through biomass alone, and the density of OFL values changes slope at that point.

```{r ofl-distribution, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, fig.width=6.5, fig.height=3.4, out.width="80%", fig.cap="Probability distribution of the 2026/27 overfishing limit from the recommended Tier 4 model (morphometrically mature male biomass, the sloped crab-FMP control rule, and the Baranov catch equation), obtained by propagating the REMA 95 percent confidence interval on the terminal smoothed survey biomass through the control rule and the catch equation. The dashed line is the recommended OFL. The shaded band is the central 95 percent confidence interval."}
if (!is.null(ofl_draws)) {
  .pos <- ofl_draws[ofl_draws > 0]
  .op  <- par(mar = c(4.2, 4.2, 0.6, 0.8))
  .dd  <- density(.pos)
  plot(.dd, main = "", xlab = "OFL (1,000 t)", ylab = "Density",
       xlim = c(0, max(ofl_2026_uci * 1.12, as.numeric(quantile(.pos, 0.995)))),
       lwd = 1.4)
  .in <- .dd$x >= ofl_2026_lci & .dd$x <= ofl_2026_uci
  polygon(c(ofl_2026_lci, .dd$x[.in], ofl_2026_uci),
          c(0, .dd$y[.in], 0), col = "grey85", border = NA)
  lines(.dd, lwd = 1.4)
  abline(v = ofl_2026, lty = 2)
  par(.op)
} else {
  plot.new(); text(0.5, 0.5, "OFL distribution not yet computed", cex = 1.1)
}
```

## Models presented {-}

This assessment evaluated `r n_models` Tier 3 models. `Model 26.1b` is the author-preferred Tier 3 model: it includes the corrections endorsed by the CPT in May 2026 and the SSC in June 2026 and is fit to the most recent data. Two sensitivities examine the removal of the female population and the truncation of the data to 2019. However, given continued convergence problems, none of the models presented is proposed for the 2026/27 specification. They are presented to document progress on the convergence problems. Jittering `Model 26.1b` located six minima, and the fit included here was the best any jitter achieved, and it was reached by `r jit_fmt(jit_n_at_base, 0)` of the `r jit_fmt(jit_n_conv, 0)` jitter runs that converged. The separation in likelihood is small but the management quantities differ materially. Removing the female population improves that markedly, with 25.3 percent of the jitter runs achieving the minimum, and is the most promising direction identified this cycle. Four additional model sensitivities built to diagnose the convergence problems (`26.d1` stability, `26.d3` eqmdevs, `26.d4` combined, and `26.d5` male-only with eqmdevs) are reported in Appendix B. They are structural experiments, not candidate assessment models.

\newpage

# A. Summary of Major Changes

1. **Management:** The eastern Bering Sea snow crab population was declared overfished in October 2021 and the directed fishery was closed by the State of Alaska for the 2022 and 2023 seasons. A small fishery occurred in 2024, with 2.15 kt retained, and a larger one in 2025, with 4.13 kt retained. The stock remains under a rebuilding plan.

2. **Input data:** The 2026 NMFS summer trawl survey and the 2025/26 fishery data were added. Four corrections were made to the input data. The total-male size composition was corrected, resolving a discrepancy between the file used in September 2025 and the file produced by the script that processes the ADF&G data. The plus group was expanded to include all crab greater than 135 mm carapace width, which the previous assessments excluded. The size-composition bin convention was changed so that a crab falling exactly on a 5 mm cutoff is assigned to the upper bin. A transcription error in the growth data was corrected (a 26.3 mm crab's molt increment was recorded as 73 mm instead of 7.3 mm). Hybrid *Chionoecetes* catch and survey data were evaluated in the May 2026 preliminary assessment and are not included in any model presented here, following CPT and SSC advice. An immature survey index was likewise evaluated and is not brought forward.

3. **Assessment methodology:** The Tier 4 model is a random-effects (REMA) model in which the averaging period for the Tier 4 B~MSY~ proxy was extended to the full survey time series, 1982 to 2026 (the September 2025 assessment averaged 1982 to 2024). This changes the proxy for morphometrically mature males to `r .f(bmsy_2026, 2)` kt and stock status to `r .f(status_2026, 3)`, compared with 148.18 kt and 0.769 on the earlier window, and lowers the minimum stock size threshold. Under the ramped control rule the proxy enters the OFL through stock status, so the wider window also changes the recommended OFL slightly (Section F). Following the June 2026 SSC recommendation, the Tier 4 model is recommended as the basis for the harvest specification until a simpler and more stable Tier 3 model is developed. The Tier 3 models are presented to document progress and are not proposed for specification.

    The Tier 3 models presented are size-based, integrated assessments using GMACS, version 2.20.34, fit using maximum likelihood. Retrospective and jittering analyses were performed for four of the six models presented (Tables \@ref(tab:model-overview) and \@ref(tab:retro-rho)). Model 25.3 and Model 26.1a were not re-run for either. The probability of terminal molt at size now comes from the maturity workflow developed by the Kodiak laboratory (Ryznar, in prep), replacing the design-based series used previously. Every fit used additional Newton steps using the inverse Hessian, which reduces the maximum gradient to zero without materially moving the fit.

4. **Assessment results:** Following SSC direction, the 2026/27 harvest specification is presented under the Tier 4 model using morphometrically mature male biomass, applying the sloped crab FMP control rule and the Baranov catch equation. Estimated mature male biomass is `r .f(mmb_2026, 2)` kt against a B~MSY~ proxy of `r .f(bmsy_2026, 2)` kt, a stock status of `r .f(status_2026, 3)`, giving F~OFL~ = `r .f(fofl_2026, 3)` yr^-1^ under the control rule. The OFL is `r .f(ofl_2026, 2)` kt, and the ABC after a `r sprintf("%.0f", 100*(1-ABC_buffer))` percent buffer is `r .f(abc_2026, 2)` kt. For comparison with 2025, the like-for-like basis is the 2025 Tier 4 assessment using the same maturity definition, which gave an OFL of `r .f(ofl_2025_tier4_morph, 2)` kt using a flat F = M rate and the linear catch equation. The same basis on this cycle's data gives `r .f(ofl_2026_linear, 2)` kt, a change of `r if (is.na(ofl_2026_linear)) "[[not yet computed]]" else sprintf("%.0f", 100*(ofl_2026_linear/ofl_2025_tier4_morph - 1))` percent from the data update alone. The OFL is lower because this cycle applies the sloped control rule and the Baranov catch equation (Section F). The specification the SSC adopted for 2025/26 was an OFL of 20.11 kt and an ABC of 12.07 kt under Tier 4b.

\newpage

# B. Responses to SSC and CPT comments

Comments are reproduced below in italics and grouped by the meeting at which they were made, most recent first. The two most recent sets of comments from each body are covered in full: the June 2026 and October 2025 SSC reports, and the May 2026 and September 2025 Crab Plan Team reports. Selected earlier comments are retained where the request is still open.

***2026(6) SSC.** The SSC recommends that the author only bring the Tier 4 model forward in October, to allow more time for development of a simpler, viable Tier 3 model.*

The recommended overfishing limit and acceptable biological catch are calculated under Tier 4 (Section F). `r n_models` Tier 3 models are presented to document progress on the convergence problems and are not proposed for specification. The type and purpose of each is stated in Table \@ref(tab:model-overview).


***2026(6) SSC.** The SSC supports bringing forward the composition correction and the expanded plus group in future models, as these appear to be clear technical improvements and corrections to the treatment of size compositions (>135 mm carapace width) that were previously ignored.*

Both corrections are included in every model presented here other than the rolled-forward 2025 model, which is reported as originally fitted. Their derivation is described in Section A. They enter the model set at `Model 26.1`, the first step from the rolled-forward 2025 model (Section E).


***2026(6) SSC.** The SSC agrees with the CPT that the immature survey index should not be treated as a convergence fix by itself. Although it may remove the visible bimodality in jitters, it also appears to shift the model toward higher natural mortality among mature males and unstable reference point behavior. Importantly, there is a clear question of whether this represents a duplicative use of the same survey data within the model.*

The immature survey index is not included in any model presented here. The underlying question of what generates the multiple minima is unresolved and is listed among the research priorities in Section I.


***2026(6) SSC.** The SSC notes that, with a new lead author, this may be an opportunity to strip the model down to a minimal parameter set that avoids convergence issues and then add back biological or process features as needed while maintaining model stability. This sequential approach to increasing model complexity by unfixing (estimating) parameters can be informed by the existing correlations among parameters in Model 25.2c.*

`Model 26.2` is a first step in this direction. Removing the female population reduces the estimated parameter count from 412 to 234 and improves the numerical behavior of the model markedly (Section E). It is presented as a sensitivity, not as a candidate for specification. A staged simplification of the male-only model, removing parameters in sequence and testing convergence at each step, has not been carried out and is the obvious next step.


***2026(6) SSC.** For potential new Tier 3 models brought forward in 2027, the SSC recommends that the assessment include a focused convergence section that identifies which parameters separate the jitter clouds, including correlation diagnostics, likelihood profiles for terminal MMB, recent recruitment, M, and OFL, and targeted model simplification runs. Those simplifications should be targeted rather than broad. Examples include fixing the recruitment sex ratio at 50:50, and reducing confounding among growth, M, and selectivity.*

Partially addressed. See Model convergence and comparison in Section E. The parameters that separate the jitter minima are identified and ranked in Table \@ref(tab:jitter-attribution) and Figure \@ref(fig:jitt-attrib). Two targeted simplification runs are presented: `Model 26.2`, which removes the female population and with it the confounding among female growth, natural mortality and selectivity, and `Model 26.1c`, which tests whether the post-collapse data are the source of the problem. Jitter and retrospective analyses, in addition to convergence diagnostics, are included.


***2026(6) SSC.** The SSC continues to request a yield-per-recruit analysis that could be used to inform development of an alternative harvest control rule.*

Not completed for this cycle. See the response to the October 2025 SSC comment below, which sets out what the analysis is to contain. This will be conducted for the September 2027 assessment.


***2026(6) SSC.** The SSC recommends that future snow crab SAFEs include a “Rebuilding Analysis and Update” section as appropriate, given the stock’s 2021 overfished determination.*

Section H reports the status of the rebuilding plan adopted under Amendment 53, its relationship to the two earlier plans, and progress toward the rebuilt threshold on the basis used for the specification.


***2026(6) SSC.** The SSC agrees with the CPT that it is premature to include hybrid catch data in the snow and Tanner crab assessment models … the SSC agrees that uncertainties associated with hybrids can be accounted for in existing buffer setting processes for Tanner and snow crab, though the SSC cautions against a predetermined direction in modifying any buffer, recognizing this uncertainty could go either way.*

No hybrid catch or survey data are included in any model presented here. Hybrid-related uncertainty is accounted for in the risk table (Table \@ref(tab:risk-table)) and in the buffer discussion in Section G. The two outstanding data problems, identification consistency between ADF&G and NMFS and the apportionment of retained catch between snow crab and hybrids, are listed in Section I.


***2026(5) CPT.** The base model brought forward was model 25.3 (which was mistakenly labeled as model 25 in the proposed model document and presentation), the author- and CPT-recommended model from 2025 … Numbers for new models that were brought forward at this meeting were mistakenly labeled as corresponding to 2025 rather than 2026, and this will be corrected for the September CPT meeting.*

The models are renumbered accordingly. The 2025 accepted assessment is `Model 25.3`, and the runs introduced in May 2026 are numbered 26.x. The correspondence with the numbering used in the May 2026 preliminary assessment is given under Model scenarios in Section E, because the June 2026 SSC report refers to the accepted configuration by its May number, `Model 25.2c` (`Model 26.1` here), and the review checklist asks that model numbers be cross-validated against those the SSC endorsed.


***2026(5) CPT.** The CPT noted that the authors did not present an analysis the CPT had previously requested: a model run with only data through 2019 to test the hypothesis that the model convergence problems stem from difficulties estimating recruitment following the population crash and the lack of 2020 survey data … The CPT continues to request this analysis as the authors seek to understand the causes of the convergence problems.*

This analysis is presented as `Model 26.1c` (Section E). Truncating the data did not resolve the convergence problem. The 2019 model converges more often and more of its runs meet the conventional gradient criterion, but it settles into ten distinct minima instead of six, and only 1.1 percent of converged runs recover the best fit, against 1.3 percent for the full model. The absence of the 2020 survey is therefore not the source of the multimodality.


***2026(5) CPT.** As an additional step to investigate the convergence problems, the CPT recommended that the authors take the following approach: fix most of the model parameters that can be fixed, confirm that the model run with very few parameters converges, then add estimation of parameters sequentially and evaluate when convergence fails. The CPT also recommended that the authors look at the parameter covariance matrix, pull out the top two or three parameters that are highly correlated, and explore the effects of those parameters on model convergence.*

Neither exercise has been completed. `Model 26.2` removes 178 estimated parameters at once and demonstrates that a substantially smaller model is better behaved, but that is a single large reduction, not the sequential procedure the CPT described. The parameters separating the jitter minima were identified from the jitter runs themselves (Table \@ref(tab:jitter-attribution)), not from the estimated covariance matrix. This will be conducted for the January 2027 modeling workshop.


***2026(5) CPT.** For September 2026, the CPT would like to see the following: Tier 4 analysis … Model 25.2c … Model 25.2c with only males included.*

All three are presented. The Tier 4 model is presented in Section F and is the basis for the recommended harvest specification. `Model 26.1` is included as the step-change baseline, and `Model 26.2` is the male-only sensitivity, requested by the CPT to test whether simplifying the model in this way might resolve the persistent convergence problems. It substantially reduces them without removing them (Section E).


***2026(5) CPT.** The CPT recommended that future Tier 3 models for the snow crab stock should include all three of these error corrections* [the total-male size composition, the sizes included in the plus group, and the new maturity workflow]*.*

All three are included in every September Tier 3 model other than the rolled-forward 2025 model. `Model 26.1a` isolates the effect of the size-composition binning convention and the growth transcription error against the May baseline.


***2026(5) CPT.** The CPT did not request that model runs including hybrids be brought forward for September 2026, due to their small influence on output in the sensitivity runs and the larger issues in the Tier 3 snow crab models that need to be resolved.*

No hybrid model is presented. The May 2026 hybrid candidates and their results remain available in the preliminary assessment document.


***2025(10) SSC.** Snow crab was declared overfished in 2021, but the SAFE did not include a section on “Rebuilding Analysis and Update.” The SSC recommends that this section be included in future SAFEs as appropriate.*

Section H reports progress toward rebuilding against the 2026 survey, together with the definition of the rebuilt threshold, the rebuilding period, and the projections underlying it.


***2025(10) SSC.** The SSC considered convergence problems with Model 25.3 to be severe enough to prevent its use for harvest recommendations. Due to this uncertainty, the SSC recommends the Tier 4 approach using mature male biomass as a fallback until the Tier 3 model's convergence and identifiability are clearly improved … The SSC intends this be a temporary approach until an acceptable Tier 3 model can be developed.*

The recommended harvest specification is calculated under Tier 4 on morphometrically mature male biomass, following this recommendation and the June 2026 SSC recommendation that only the Tier 4 model be brought forward. Results for the large-male (>= 95 mm) and preferred-male (> 101 mm) definitions are reported for comparison (Table \@ref(tab:tier4-currencies)) but are not the basis of the recommendation. Convergence and identifiability of the Tier 3 model improved on several diagnostics this cycle, but the multiple minima persist, so the Tier 4 approach remains the author-recommended basis for management advice.


***2025(10) SSC.** The SSC recommends that the assessment author explore strategies to constrain the model complexity during this period. For example, reducing the number of years with increased natural mortality may provide the model enough constraint to allow model convergence. More generally, the snow crab assessment would likely benefit from a decrease in flexibility to ensure convergence and stable, interpretable parameter estimates and results.*

`Model 26.2` addresses this by removing the female population and 178 of the 412 estimated parameters. It is the best-behaved model on the diagnostic most relevant here: 25.3 percent of converged jitter runs recover its own best fit, against 1.1 to 6.1 percent for the other three models jittered (Section E). The number of mortality-event years has not been reduced; both 2018 and 2019 are retained in all models. The second immature-female mortality block is the one parameter clearly not identified from these data, and whether to fix it is put to the Plan Team under Model convergence and comparison. Experiments that fix it are reported in Appendix B (26.d1 and 26.d4); fixing it did not resolve the multimodality. A single-mortality-event run has not been evaluated.


***2025(10) SSC.** Table 13 also raises questions about what is actually being fit in the GMACS model. A significant number of parameters are either showing estimates of zero or are estimated identically to other parameters. If it is true that these parameters are active and being estimated, that would clearly cause some of the pathologies seen in the jitter analysis.*

The estimated parameters of the accepted fit of `Model 26.1b` are examined under Model convergence and comparison in Section E. Twenty-four of the 412 estimated parameters have a standard error larger than the absolute value of the estimate. Sixteen of those are deviation or offset parameters estimated within 0.1 of zero, for which a large ratio is expected and not diagnostic. No parameter reached a bound, and the Hessian has no non-positive eigenvalues. Further analysis on parameter identifiability will be conducted in the January 2027 modeling workshop.


***2025(10) SSC.** To explore development of an ABC control rule, the SSC requests that a yield per recruit analysis be developed for snow crab. This analysis should graph the yield per recruit as a function of fishing mortality, along with associated reductions in various stock metrics, including mature male biomass and male biomass >95 mm. Show the F~0.1~ fishing mortality rate … The SSC is still interested in developing a wider range of options for reference points for snow crab rather than entirely abandoning morphometric male maturity per recruit. For example, as an interim measure, adopting a more conservative F~SPR~ proxy (e.g., F~65%~) would keep the control rule tied to biology. It would also be of interest to explore a two-sex, fertilized-egg SPR analysis (“fathers matter”) so spawning output reflects male abundance/size-dependent fertilization.*

This analysis has not been produced for this cycle, and the request was repeated by the SSC in June 2026. Given the transition in authors, this was not conducted this cycle and will be presented in 2027.


***2025(10) SSC.** The SSC requests an exploration of whether the estimated large differences in male and female recruitment years could be related to the lack of fit to molt-increment data.*

Not undertaken. The growth data and the model fits to them are shown in Figure \@ref(fig:growthfits), and a transcription error in the growth data has been corrected this cycle (Section A), but the relationship between the fit to molt increment and the divergence between male and female recruitment years has not been examined. The male-only model removes the question instead of answering it.


***2025(10) SSC.** As with a similar SSC recommendation for Tanner crab, the SSC recommends consideration of different inclusions/exclusions of hybrids into the snow crab assessment (i.e., in survey and catch data) to evaluate sensitivity to these options and ensure an internally consistent approach.*

The May 2026 preliminary assessment evaluated including hybrids in both the survey and fishery data; the effect on management advice was minor. The CPT in May 2026 and the SSC in June 2026 both concluded hybrid data should not be included at this time, and no hybrid model is brought forward. One data problem remains: retained catch already contains both hybrids and snow crab with no method to separate them, so the retained series is identical between configurations. That unaccounted removal is a source of uncertainty in the OFL and bears on the ABC buffer in Section G. The June 2026 SSC cautioned against a predetermined direction in modifying the buffer.


***2025(10) SSC.** The SSC recommends that research be conducted to evaluate whether clutch fullness is a reliable indicator of female reproductive output, using histology or lab rearing experiments.*

This has been added to the list of priority laboratory studies.


***2025(10) SSC.** The SSC is willing to participate in a collaborative working group during spring 2026 to facilitate additional progress on the development of an ABC control rule for snow crab.*

We appreciate the SSC’s willingness to collaborate.


***2025(10) SSC.** The SSC also reiterates its general comments from December 2024 suggesting that authors use likelihood profiles to describe uncertainty in model parameters and management quantities and use jittering analyses only to ensure that the results provided come from the model with the lowest negative log likelihood (the “MLE”).*

Jittering was done for four of the six models presented (Table \@ref(tab:model-overview)), and the accepted fit of each jittered model is the run with the lowest negative log likelihood among its jitters, which is the use of jittering the SSC describes. Likelihood profiles have not been produced. These will be produced once a stable, converged model is identified.

***2025(10) SSC.** The SSC recommends that morphometric maturity status be overlaid on the size distribution plots (Figure 9) to allow visual tracking of growth and the transition to maturity by cohort.*

The figure below plots the abundance of immature and mature male crab at size observed in the survey by year, through the 2026 survey, with maturity assigned by the new workflow the CPT recommended for adoption in May 2026.

     regenerates from the current survey pull: "Numbers at size by maturity state
     by year" (02 :472-475) -- the same immature/mature-at-size-by-year content the
     paragraph above describes, but on 2026 data rather than last cycle's. -->
