# Mohn's rho, written by 06_run_retrospective.R (retro_rho loaded in retro-setup).
## All four models with retrospective sweeps; falls back to the accepted model
## alone if the combined frame could not be built.
.rt <- if (exists("retro_all") && !is.null(retro_all)) retro_all else
  if (!is.null(retro_rho)) cbind(Model = as.character(to_short(accepted_model)),
                                 retro_rho, stringsAsFactors = FALSE) else NULL
if (is.null(.rt)) {
  cat("*Retrospective results not yet generated; run `06_run_retrospective.R`.*")
} else {
  rho_tab <- data.frame(
    Model = .rt$Model,
    Quantity = c(mature_male_biomass = "Mature male biomass",
                 recruitment_male    = "Male recruitment")[.rt$quantity],
    Retrospective = c(standard    = "Standard",
                      drop_survey = "Terminal survey dropped")[.rt$mode],
    Peels          = .rt$n_peels,
    MohnsRho       = round(.rt$mohns_rho, 3),
    RalstonsSigma  = round(.rt$ralstons_sigma, 3),
    MinRel         = round(.rt$min_rel_diff, 3),
    MaxRel         = round(.rt$max_rel_diff, 3),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE, row.names = NULL
  )
  ## Biomass rows before recruitment rows within each model.
  rho_tab <- rho_tab[order(rho_tab$Model,
                           match(rho_tab$Quantity,
                                 c("Mature male biomass", "Male recruitment")),
                           rho_tab$Retrospective), ]
  colnames(rho_tab) <- c("Model", "Quantity", "Retrospective", "Peels", "Mohn's rho",
                         "Ralston's sigma", "Min rel. diff.", "Max rel. diff.")

  flextable::flextable(rho_tab) |>
    flextable::fontsize(size = 8, part = "all") |>
  # Straddles a page break, so flextable repeats the caption and its \label in
  # the longtable continuation head and the label is reported as multiply
  # defined. Keep caption and label on the first page only (2026-08-31).
  flextable::set_table_properties(opts_pdf = list(caption_repeat = FALSE)) |>
    flextable::autofit() |>
    ## Rescale to the 6.5 in portrait line; autofit alone sized this table
    ## wider than the page and clipped the right-hand columns (2026-09-08).
    flextable::fit_to_width(max_width = 6.4) |>
    flextable::set_caption(
      caption = paste("Retrospective statistics for the four models with retrospective sweeps this cycle. Mohn's rho",
      "and Ralston's sigma are dimensionless. Mohn's rho is the mean over peels of (peel - full",
      "model) / full model at each peel's terminal year, so a positive value means terminal estimates",
      "are revised downward as data accumulate. Ralston's sigma is the log-scale RMSE of the same",
      "pairs. Dropped-terminal-survey peels are compared with the full model. Peels for Models 26.1c",
      "and 26.1 are relative to their own terminal years, 2019 and 2024."),
      autonum = officer::run_autonum(seq_id = "tab", pre_label = "Table ", bkm = "retro-rho")
    )
}

```{r obscatch, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=F}
# 1. Extract and combine data from multiple cases
catch_comparison <- case_for_data_table %>%
  purrr::map_dfr(function(case_name) {
    reslst$repsLst[[case_name]]$Catch_fit_summary %>%
      dplyr::transmute(
        Model = case_name,
        Year = as.numeric(year),
        # Create descriptive labels for the catch categories
        Category = dplyr::case_when(
          type == "retained" ~ "Retained (kt)",
          type == "discarded" & sex == "female" ~ "Discard Female",
          type == "discarded" & sex == "male" & fleet == "Pot_Fishery" ~ "Discard Male Pot",
          fleet == "Trawl_Bycatch" ~ "Non-directed Bycatch",
          TRUE ~ paste(type, sex, fleet)
        ),
        obs = as.numeric(obs)
      )
  })

# 2. Pivot so each catch category appears once per model.
# The two models in case_for_data_table are the 2025 rolled-forward reference and
# the author-recommended model. Until 2026-08-29 this block labeled the SECOND of
# them " + hybrids" -- a survival from the May bracket, where the pair really was
# base vs hybrid. Neither September model contains hybrid data, so the table was
# presenting the recommended model's discards to the reader as a hybrid run. The
# columns are now labeled with the models' own shortnames, which is also what
# makes the table informative: it shows how the observed catch inputs changed
# between the 2025 assessment and this one.
PlotTab <- catch_comparison %>%
  mutate(Model = as.character(to_short(Model))) %>%
  # Retained catch and non-directed bycatch are the same series in both models
  # for every year the earlier model covers, so carry them once, from the
  # recommended model, which also supplies the terminal year.
  dplyr::filter(!(Model == to_short(case_for_data_table[1]) &
                    Category %in% c("Retained (kt)", "Non-directed Bycatch"))) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    names_from  = c(Category, Model),
    values_from = obs,
    names_sep   = ", "
  ) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(Year)

# A gap after the pivot means one of two different things, and they must not be
# printed the same way. Inside a model's own year span it means the fishery took
# nothing -- the 2022 and 2023 closures -- and belongs in the table as 0. Outside
# it, the model simply does not extend that far: Model 25.3 ends in 2024, so its
# 2025 cells are not zero catch, they are no data. A blanket is.na() <- 0 printed
# 0.00 for both (fixed 2026-08-29).
.span <- vapply(case_for_data_table, function(cs)
  max(as.numeric(reslst$repsLst[[cs]]$Catch_fit_summary$year), na.rm = TRUE),
  numeric(1))
names(.span) <- as.character(to_short(case_for_data_table))
for (nm in setdiff(names(PlotTab), "Year")) {
  .mdl <- sub("^.*, ", "", nm)                     # "" for the shared columns
  .end <- if (.mdl %in% names(.span)) .span[[.mdl]] else max(.span)
  .fill <- is.na(PlotTab[[nm]]) & PlotTab$Year <= .end
  PlotTab[[nm]][.fill] <- 0
}

# Retained catch and non-directed bycatch come from one model only, so drop the
# model suffix from those two columns; the four discard columns keep theirs.
.acc <- as.character(to_short(case_for_data_table[2]))
names(PlotTab)[names(PlotTab) == paste0("Retained (kt), ", .acc)]        <- "Retained"
names(PlotTab)[names(PlotTab) == paste0("Non-directed Bycatch, ", .acc)] <- "Non-directed bycatch"

# Column order: the shared series first, then each discard series with the
# reference model beside the recommended one.
.want <- c("Year", "Retained", "Non-directed bycatch",
           paste0("Discard Male Pot, ",   as.character(to_short(case_for_data_table))),
           paste0("Discard Female, ",     as.character(to_short(case_for_data_table))))
stopifnot("obscatch: expected columns are missing" = all(.want %in% names(PlotTab)))
PlotTab <- PlotTab[, .want]

# Compact headers. The table is 44 crab years, so it wants to stay PORTRAIT --
# landscape buys width but costs height and pushed it from two pages to three,
# which duplicated its caption a second time. Shortening the headers instead
# keeps it inside the portrait line width. The models are named in the caption.
names(PlotTab) <- sub("^Discard Male Pot, Model ",   "Male disc. ",   names(PlotTab))
names(PlotTab) <- sub("^Discard Female, Model ",     "Female disc. ", names(PlotTab))
names(PlotTab)[names(PlotTab) == "Non-directed bycatch"] <- "Bycatch"

# 3. Render with flextable + run_autonum so the Word caption carries a SEQ
#    field that \@ref(tab:obscatch) can target. Year is an integer, not a
#    measurement: colformat_int() stops flextable printing it as "1,982".
# Year must be an integer column before it reaches flextable. As a double it
# slips past colformat_int() and is then caught by colformat_double(), which
# printed the crab year as "2,013.00" (fixed 2026-08-29). Restrict the double
# formatter to the catch columns for the same reason.
PlotTab$Year <- as.integer(PlotTab$Year)
.numcols <- setdiff(names(PlotTab), "Year")

flextable::flextable(PlotTab) |>
  # 44 crab years, so this table always breaks across pages. flextable repeats
  # the caption in the longtable continuation head, which repeats the \label
  # with it and makes \@ref(tab:obscatch) ambiguous; caption_repeat = FALSE
  # keeps the caption (and the label) on the first page only (2026-08-29).
  flextable::set_table_properties(opts_pdf = list(caption_repeat = FALSE)) |>
  flextable::colformat_int(j = "Year", big.mark = "") |>
  flextable::colformat_double(j = .numcols, digits = 2, na_str = "–") |>
  flextable::fontsize(size = 8, part = "all") |>
  flextable::autofit() |>
  flextable::set_caption(
    caption = paste0(
      "Observed catch used in the assessment (1,000 t), by crab year. Retained ",
      "catch and non-directed bycatch are common to both models. Male and female ",
      "pot-fishery discards are shown for ", as.character(to_short(case_for_data_table[1])),
      " and ", as.character(to_short(case_for_data_table[2])),
      ", so that the effect of the revised ADF&G data on the discard series ",
      "is visible. The two models are otherwise fit to the same removals. A zero ",
      "is no catch (the directed fishery was closed in 2022 and 2023). A ",
      "dash means the model's data do not extend to that year."),
    autonum = officer::run_autonum(seq_id = "tab", pre_label = "Table ", bkm = "obscatch")
  )

```{r stepchange, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=F}
# Define the target management parameters to extract
# We map the GMACS label to the column index based on your logic:
# BMSY, Status, FMSY usually in index 3; FOFL, OFL in index 4.
mgmt_targets <- list(
  "BMSY"   = 3,
  "Bcurr/BMSY" = 3,
  "Fmsy"   = 4,
  "Fofl"   = 4,
  "OFL"    = 3
)

# Helper function to extract management quantities from one model folder
extract_mgmt_quantities <- function(path, model_name) {
  out_file <- file.path(path, "Gmacsall.out")
  if (!file.exists(out_file)) return(NULL)

  tmp <- readLines(out_file)

  # Identify the summary block
  st  <- grep("BMSY", tmp)[1]
  end <- grep("Ofl", tmp) |> tail(1)
  mgmt_block <- tmp[st:end]

  # Extract values based on targets
  values <- lapply(names(mgmt_targets), function(target) {
    line <- mgmt_block[grep(target, mgmt_block)][1]
    if (is.na(line)) return(NA)

    # Split by one or more spaces
    parts <- unlist(strsplit(trimws(line), " "))
    idx   <- mgmt_targets[[target]]
    return(as.numeric(parts[idx]))
  })

  names(values) <- names(mgmt_targets)

  # Extract male natural mortality (immature and mature) for the most recent
  # year. M is constant across the 22 size classes, so the first size-class
  # column is sufficient.
  m_start <- grep("Natural_mortality-by-class: dataframe", tmp, fixed = TRUE)[1]
  m_imm <- NA_real_
  m_mat <- NA_real_
  if (!is.na(m_start)) {
    eod_rel <- grep(">EOD<", tmp[(m_start + 1):length(tmp)], fixed = TRUE)[1]
    m_end <- m_start + eod_rel - 1          # last DATA line, EOD is m_start + eod_rel
    # Was (m_end - 1), which dropped that last data line. In a two-sex model the
    # dropped row is the terminal year's immature FEMALE, so the male lookup
    # below still found what it wanted and the bug was invisible; in the
    # male-only model it is the terminal immature MALE, and the table rendered a
    # silent NA for M (imm males). Fixed 2026-08-29.
    m_block <- tmp[(m_start + 2):m_end]
    m_df <- utils::read.table(text = m_block, header = FALSE,
                              stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    colnames(m_df)[1:4] <- c("Year", "Sex", "Maturity", "M")
    males <- m_df[m_df$Sex == "male", ]
    latest <- max(males$Year, na.rm = TRUE)
    m_imm <- males$M[males$Year == latest & males$Maturity == "immature"][1]
    m_mat <- males$M[males$Year == latest & males$Maturity == "mature"][1]
  }
  values[["M (imm males)"]] <- as.numeric(m_imm)
  values[["M (mat males)"]] <- as.numeric(m_mat)

  # Terminal-year MMB and average recruitment. The checklist requires both in
  # this table and the caption already described them, but neither was extracted
  # (added 2026-08-29).
  #
  # MMB is the SSB column of the Overall_summary block in its last year. That it
  # is biomass at MATING, not at the survey, is not merely assumed: Model 25.3's
  # terminal value, 137.4593369, is identical to the 2024 entry of the 2025
  # vintage in data/historical/historical_mmb_mating_by_assessment.csv.
  #
  # Average recruitment is GMACS's own `Male Spr_rbar`, i.e. the mean male
  # recruitment over the window the SPR reference points are computed on, so it
  # is the average that belongs beside B_MSY rather than one recomputed here.
  s_start <- grep("^Summary: dataframe", tmp)[1]
  term_yr <- NA_real_; mmb_term <- NA_real_
  if (!is.na(s_start)) {
    s_rows <- character(0)
    for (ln in tmp[(s_start + 2):length(tmp)]) {
      if (!nzchar(trimws(ln)) || startsWith(ln, ">")) break
      s_rows <- c(s_rows, ln)
    }
    if (length(s_rows)) {
      last <- strsplit(trimws(tail(s_rows, 1)), " +")[[1]]
      term_yr  <- as.numeric(last[1])
      mmb_term <- as.numeric(last[2])
    }
  }
  rbar_line <- grep("^Male Spr_rbar", tmp, value = TRUE)[1]
  rbar <- if (is.na(rbar_line)) NA_real_ else
    as.numeric(strsplit(trimws(rbar_line), " +")[[1]][4]) / 1e6

  values[["Terminal year"]]  <- term_yr
  values[["MMB (terminal)"]] <- mmb_term
  values[["Avg recruitment"]] <- rbar

  return(dplyr::as_tibble(values) |> dplyr::mutate(Model = model_name))
}

# Iterate over the models this cycle ran, not the retained May bracket -- this is
# the table the OFL/BMSY comparison is read from, so a row per non-existent model
# would put NA management quantities in front of the CPT.
ref_table <- names(models_present) |>
  purrr::map_dfr(~extract_mgmt_quantities(models_present[.x], .x)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(Model = to_short(Model)) |>
  dplyr::arrange(Model) |>          # model_order, not folder order (0-models.R)
  dplyr::select(Model, everything()) # Reorder to put Model first

# Render with flextable so \@ref(tab:stepchange) resolves in Word output.
# Terminal year is a year, not a measurement. Left as a double it is caught by
# colformat_double() and printed "2,024.00", so make it an integer and keep the
# double formatter off it -- the same trap as the Year column of Table
# \@ref(tab:obscatch).
ref_table$`Terminal year` <- as.integer(ref_table$`Terminal year`)

flextable::flextable(ref_table) |>
  flextable::colformat_int(j = "Terminal year", big.mark = "") |>
  flextable::colformat_double(j = setdiff(names(ref_table), c("Model", "Terminal year")),
                              digits = 2) |>
  flextable::fontsize(size = 7, part = "all") |>
  flextable::autofit() |>
  ## Rescale to the 6.5 in portrait line; autofit alone sized this table
  ## wider than the page and clipped the right-hand columns (2026-09-08).
  flextable::fit_to_width(max_width = 6.4) |>
  flextable::set_caption(
    caption = paste("Management quantities by model, from maximum likelihood estimates using Tier 3",
      "reference points. Biomass and OFL in 1,000 t; natural mortality per year; average recruitment",
      "in billions. M is for immature and mature males in each model's terminal year; Model 26.1c",
      "terminates in 2019, itself a mortality-event year, so its M is an event value and not",
      "comparable. MMB is at mating in that terminal year. Status is Bcurr/BMSY, Bcurr being the",
      "projected biomass the control rule acts on. Average recruitment is GMACS Spr_rbar for males.",
      "The Fmsy and Fofl columns are GMACS fleet-1 values, not annual instantaneous rates."),
    autonum = officer::run_autonum(seq_id = "tab", pre_label = "Table ", bkm = "stepchange")
  )

```{r predsurvbio, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=F}
## Enabled 2026-09-08: one of the three tables (17-19 in the September 2025
## document) that reviewers and the public ask for, per C. Szuwalski. The
## Gmacsall.out section headers parsed below are the GMACS 2.20.34 format,
## which is the version used throughout this assessment.
# --- 1. Extract Weight and Results ---
# Direct indexing instead of eval(parse)
rep_obj     <- reslst$repsLst[[names(report_model)]]
weight_data <- rep_obj$IndivWeightByXM

# Extract weight-at-length vectors (assuming 22 size classes)
male_wt   <- weight_data |> 
  dplyr::filter(Sex == "male", Year == 1982, Maturity == 'mature') |> 
  dplyr::select(matches("^[0-9]")) |> as.numeric()

female_wt <- weight_data |> 
  dplyr::filter(Sex == "female", Year == 1982, Maturity == 'mature') |> 
  dplyr::select(matches("^[0-9]")) |> as.numeric()

# --- 2. Extract Population Numbers (N) ---
# Helper to extract dataframe sections from Gmacsall.out without manual loops
extract_gmacs_df <- function(lines, header) {
  start <- grep(header, lines, fixed = TRUE) + 1
  end   <- grep("EOD", lines[start:length(lines)])[1] + start - 2
  read.table(text = lines[start:end])
}

gmacs_lines <- readLines(file.path(report_model, "/Gmacsall.out"))
n_males_mat <- extract_gmacs_df(gmacs_lines, "N(males_mature): dataframe")
n_females_mat <- extract_gmacs_df(gmacs_lines, "N(females_mature): dataframe")

# --- 3. Extract Selectivity ---
dfrSel <- wtsGMACS::extractRep1Results(reslst, "selfcns") |> 
  dplyr::filter(type == "capture", fleet == "NMFS_Trawl_1989", 
                case == names(report_model), sex == 'male', year == 2023)

# Ensure selectivity vector length matches size classes (22)
male_sel <- dfrSel |> 
  dplyr::select(matches("^[0-9]")) |> as.numeric()

# --- 4. Define Size Filters ---
# Logic for biomass/abundance tiers based on carapace width (CW)
sizes <- seq(27.5, 132.5, 5)
mask_95  <- ifelse(sizes >= 95, 1.0, 0.0)

# User-specific logic for >105mm: 
# Includes 50% of the 97.5 bin
# Standardizing to the logic in your snippet:
mask_101 <- dplyr::case_when(
  sizes > 105  ~ 1.0,
  sizes == 102.5 ~ 0.5, 
  TRUE         ~ 0.0
)


midpoints <- seq(27.5, 132.5, by = 5)

# --- 5. Vectorized Calculations ---
# Convert N dataframes to matrices (excluding Year column)
mat_males   <- as.matrix(n_males_mat[-1, -1])
mat_females <- as.matrix(n_females_mat[-1, -1])

# Calculate Biomass and Abundance (in 1,000 t or billions)
results_tab <- data.frame(
  Year = n_males_mat[-1, 1],
  MMB_95   = (mat_males %*% (male_wt * male_sel * mask_95)) / 1e6,
  MMB_101  = (mat_males %*% (male_wt * male_sel * mask_101)) / 1e6,
  Abund_101 = (mat_males %*% (male_sel * mask_101)) / 1e3,
  # Population (True Values)
  FMB_tot      = (mat_females %*% female_wt) / 1e6,
  MMB_tot      = (mat_males %*% male_wt) / 1e6,
  MMB_95_tot   = (mat_males %*% (male_wt * mask_95)) / 1e6,
  MMB_101_tot  = (mat_males %*% (male_wt * mask_101)) / 1e6,
  Abund_101_tot = (mat_males %*% mask_101) / 1e3
)

survey_results <- data.frame(
  # Predicted (Subject to Survey Selectivity)
  Year      = wtsGMACS::extractRep1Results(reslst, "Index_fit_summary") |> 
    filter(sex == 'female', case == names(report_model)) |> pull(year),
  FMB      = wtsGMACS::extractRep1Results(reslst, "Index_fit_summary") |> 
    filter(sex == 'female', case == names(report_model)) |> pull(prd),
  MMB      = wtsGMACS::extractRep1Results(reslst, "Index_fit_summary") |> 
    filter(sex == 'male', case == names(report_model)) |> pull(prd)
)

# --- 6. Final Table Formatting ---
PlotTab <- survey_results |> 
  full_join(results_tab) |> 
  mutate(across(everything(), as.numeric)) |>
  mutate(across(-Year, ~round(.x, 2))) %>%
  select(Year, FMB, MMB, MMB_95, MMB_101, Abund_101, FMB_tot, MMB_tot, MMB_95_tot, MMB_101_tot, Abund_101_tot) %>%
  arrange(Year)

PlotTab$Year <- as.character(PlotTab$Year)  # keep 1982 from printing as 1,982
colnames(PlotTab) <- c("Year", "FMB", "MMB", "MMB >=95", "MMB >101", "N >101",
                       "FMB pop", "MMB pop", "MMB >=95 pop", "MMB >101 pop", "N >101 pop")
flextable::flextable(PlotTab) |>
  flextable::fontsize(size = 7, part = "all") |>
  flextable::align(j = 2:11, align = "right", part = "all") |>
  flextable::width(j = 1, width = 0.45) |>
  flextable::width(j = 2:11, width = 0.59) |>
  flextable::set_table_properties(layout = "fixed",
                                  opts_pdf = list(caption_repeat = FALSE)) |>
  flextable::padding(padding = 1.5, part = "all") |>
  flextable::set_caption(
    caption = paste("Maximum likelihood estimates of mature male (MMB) and female (FMB)",
                    "biomass (1,000 t) and abundance of preferred males (N >101, millions)",
                    "from Model 26.1b. Columns 2-6 are at the time of the survey and subject",
                    "to survey selectivity. Columns 7-11 (pop) are population values not",
                    "subject to selectivity."),
    autonum = officer::run_autonum(seq_id = "tab", pre_label = "Table ", bkm = "predsurvbio")
  )

```{r predtotnum, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
## Enabled 2026-09-08 (Table 18 in the September 2025 document, per C. Szuwalski).
# --- 0. Helper + load Gmacsall.out ---
# Inlined here so this chunk does not depend on the eval=FALSE chunk above.
extract_gmacs_df <- function(lines, header) {
  start <- grep(header, lines, fixed = TRUE) + 1
  end   <- grep("EOD", lines[start:length(lines)])[1] + start - 2
  read.table(text = lines[start:end])
}

gmacs_lines <- readLines(file.path(report_model, "/Gmacsall.out"))

# --- 1. Extract Data Using Helper ---
n_males   <- extract_gmacs_df(gmacs_lines, "N(males): dataframe")
n_females <- extract_gmacs_df(gmacs_lines, "N(females): dataframe")

# --- 2. Vectorized Calculation ---
# Convert to matrices and drop the first two metadata columns (Year, Season)
mat_m <- as.matrix(n_males[-1, -1])
mat_f <- as.matrix(n_females[-1, -1])

# Calculate row sums for both matrices and convert to billions
# (Assumes model units are in thousands)
total_n_billions <- (rowSums(mat_m) + rowSums(mat_f)) / 1e6

# --- 3. Final Table Assembly ---
tmp_mat <- data.frame(
  `Survey year`   = as.character(n_males[-1, 1]),
  `Total numbers` = round(total_n_billions, 2),
  check.names     = FALSE
)

# --- 4. Render Table ---
# Two year blocks side by side (same layout as the observed-biomass table) so
# the ~45 rows fit one page instead of spilling across two.
.n <- nrow(tmp_mat); .half <- ceiling(.n / 2)
.a <- tmp_mat[seq_len(.half), ]
.b <- tmp_mat[seq.int(.half + 1L, .n), ]
if (nrow(.b) < nrow(.a)) .b[seq.int(nrow(.b) + 1L, nrow(.a)), ] <- ""
names(.b) <- paste0(names(.b), " ")
tmp_mat2 <- cbind(.a, .b); rownames(tmp_mat2) <- NULL

flextable::flextable(tmp_mat2) |>
  flextable::fontsize(size = 8, part = "all") |>
  flextable::align(j = c(2, 4), align = "right", part = "all") |>
  flextable::width(j = c(1, 3), width = 0.8) |>
  flextable::width(j = c(2, 4), width = 1.4) |>
  flextable::set_table_properties(layout = "fixed",
                                  opts_pdf = list(caption_repeat = FALSE)) |>
  flextable::padding(padding = 2, part = "all") |>
  flextable::vline(j = 2, border = officer::fp_border(color = "grey55", width = 1),
                   part = "all") |>
  flextable::set_caption(
    caption = paste("Maximum likelihood estimates of total numbers of crab (billions) from",
                    "Model 26.1b, not subject to survey selectivity, at the time of the",
                    "survey. Years run down the left block and continue in the right."),
    autonum = officer::run_autonum(seq_id = "tab", pre_label = "Table ", bkm = "predtotnum")
  )

```{r predsurvbio-tot, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=F}
## Enabled 2026-09-08 (Table 19 in the September 2025 document, per C. Szuwalski).

# --- 1. Extract Summary Data for all targeted cases ---
# extractRep1Results returns a tidy dataframe containing 'case'
summary_all <- wtsGMACS::extractRep1Results(reslst, "Summary") |> 
  dplyr::filter(case %in% case_for_data_table) |> 
  dplyr::select(case, year, SSB, rec_male) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(year = as.numeric(year))

# --- 2. Extract Fishing Mortality for all targeted cases ---
# We loop through the case vector to pull the internal list objects
fm_all <- case_for_data_table |> 
  purrr::map_dfr(function(c_name) {
    rep_obj <- reslst$repsLst[[c_name]]
    
    # Identify the correct dataframe name for this specific model
    # Checks for "capture_rate" first, then "FM"
    f_df_name <- intersect(names(rep_obj), 
                           c("Fully-selected_capture_rate_by_season_sex_and_fishery", 
                             "Fully-selected_FM_by_season_sex_and_fishery"))[1]
    
    if (is.na(f_df_name)) {
      message("Warning: No F-mortality data found for case: ", c_name)
      return(NULL)
    }
    
    rep_obj[[f_df_name]] |> 
      dplyr::filter(sex == 'male', fleet == "Pot_Fishery") |> 
      dplyr::transmute(
        case = c_name,
        year = as.numeric(year),
        f_mort = as.numeric(`2`) # Directed fishing season
      )
  })

# --- 3. Join and Format for Comparison ---
# Use a join to ensure the FM and MMB align correctly for every model
sum_mat <- summary_all |>
  dplyr::inner_join(fm_all, by = c("case", "year")) |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    Model                 = as.character(to_short(case)),
    `Survey Year`         = as.character(year),
    `Mature Male Biomass` = round(as.numeric(SSB), 2),
    `Male Recruits`       = round(as.numeric(rec_male) / 1e6, 2), # Billions
    `Fishing Mortality`   = round(f_mort, 2)
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(Model, `Survey Year`)

# --- 4. Render Table ---
# One year-block per model, side by side, so the two models read as a
# comparison rather than stacking ~90 rows.
flextable::flextable(sum_mat) |>
  flextable::fontsize(size = 8, part = "all") |>
  flextable::align(j = 3:5, align = "right", part = "all") |>
  flextable::width(j = 1, width = 1.3) |>
  flextable::width(j = 2, width = 0.9) |>
  flextable::width(j = 3:5, width = 1.35) |>
  flextable::set_table_properties(layout = "fixed",
                                  opts_pdf = list(caption_repeat = FALSE)) |>
  flextable::padding(padding = 1.5, part = "all") |>
  flextable::merge_v(j = 1) |>
  flextable::valign(j = 1, valign = "top") |>
  flextable::set_caption(
    caption = paste("Comparison of mature male biomass (MMB, 1,000 t) at mating, male",
                    "recruitment (billions), and fully-selected fishing mortality (F, per",
                    "year) for the directed fishery, for the 2025 rolled-forward reference",
                    "model and the accepted model."),
    autonum = officer::run_autonum(seq_id = "tab", pre_label = "Table ", bkm = "predsurvbio-tot")
  )

DISABLED 2026-08-28. This figure compares four MAY candidates -- the immature-index

```{r surveyplots, echo=FALSE, eval=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, width = 12, height = 7, out.width="100%", fig.cap="Observed male survey biomass for models across hybrid and maturity workflow scenarios."}
dfrIndxFit_plot <- wtsGMACS::extractRep1Results(reslst, "Index_fit_summary")  %>%
  dplyr::filter(case %in% c("25.1 gmacs (update + compfix + imm_surv)", # base
                            "25.1 gmacs (update + compfix + plus group + hyb_surv)", # base + hybrid
                            "25.1 gmacs (update + compfix + plus group + new_mat + imm_surv)", # base with newmat
                            "25.1 gmacs (update + compfix + plus group + hyb_both + new_mat)") & # base + hybrid + newmat
             sex == "male" )   %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    # Categorize index
    Index_category = case_when(
      case == "25.1 gmacs (update + compfix + imm_surv)" ~ "Base",
      case ==  "25.1 gmacs (update + compfix + plus group + hyb_surv)" ~ "Base + hybrid",
      case ==  "25.1 gmacs (update + compfix + plus group + new_mat + imm_surv)" ~ "Base + newmat",
      case ==  "25.1 gmacs (update + compfix + plus group + hyb_both + new_mat)" ~ "Base + hybrid + newmat",
      .default = NA
    )) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    
    # Confidence interval calculations
    sd_log = sqrt(log(1 + as.numeric(actual_CV)^2)),
    obs = as.numeric(obs),
    lba    = qlnorm(0.05, log(obs), sd_log),
    uba    = qlnorm(0.95, log(obs), sd_log),
    year = as.numeric(year)
  )

# --- Generate the 4-Panel Plot ---
p_idx_final <- ggplot() +
  # Observations (Single black error bar per year/sex/panel)
  geom_errorbar(
    data = dfrIndxFit_plot,
    aes(x = year, ymin = lba, ymax = uba, color = Index_category), 
    width = 0.3, 
    position = position_dodge(width=0.5),
    alpha = 0.6
  ) +
  # Observations (Single black point per year/sex/panel)
  geom_point(
    data = dfrIndxFit_plot,
    position = position_dodge(width=0.5),
    aes(x = year, y = obs, color = Index_category), 
    size = 1.2
  ) +
  # Formatting and Scales
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, NA), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))) +
  labs(
    x = "Year", 
    y = "NMFS Survey Biomass (1,000 t)",
    color = "Scenario",
    subtitle = "Points/Bars: Shared Observations",
    caption = "Error bars represent 95% log-normal confidence intervals on observations."
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  facet_wrap(~maturity, ncol = 1) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.text = element_text(size = 8),
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "white"),
    panel.spacing = unit(1, "lines")
  )

print(p_idx_final)
```

\newpage


One step of this sweep adds no survey information. The peels withhold the survey through `END_YEAR` minus the peel count, so peel five ends the survey in 2020 and peel six in 2019. The 2020 survey was cancelled, and the two peels are therefore fit to the same survey series and differ only in the fishery years GMACS truncates. Their data files are byte-identical. The step between those two points on the figure should not be read as the effect of removing a survey year.

```{r rema-fit, echo=FALSE, out.width="72%", fig.cap="Random-effects (REMA) fit to the survey biomass series for each of the three Tier 4 maturity definitions: morphometrically mature males (top), males >= 95 mm (middle) and males > 101 mm (bottom). Points are the survey observations with their sampling intervals. The line and shaded band are the smoothed series and its 95 percent confidence interval. The smoothed terminal value is the biomass the control rule acts on, and the average of the smoothed series over the full time series is the B~MSY~ proxy. There is no 2020 observation because the survey was cancelled. The random-effects model supplies a value for it, which is why the average is taken over the smoothed series rather than the observations."}
knitr::include_graphics("plots/rema_tier_4_ssc.png")
```

```{r tier4-status-series, echo=FALSE, out.width="88%", fig.cap="Tier 4 stock status (biomass relative to the B~MSY~ proxy) computed on the raw survey series for the two large-male definitions. The red line is the closure threshold beta, below which the OFL is zero. The green line is half the proxy, the minimum stock size threshold. The series is shown on the raw observations rather than the smoothed fit, so it is more variable than the status reported for the specification, which is computed from the REMA fit in Figure \\@ref(fig:rema-fit)."}
knitr::include_graphics("plots/tier4_status.png")
```

```{r mmbfits, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=F, fig.width=9, fig.height=5.5, fig.cap="Model fits to the observed mature biomass at survey (1,000 t), for the five models fitted under GMACS 2.20.34. Model 25.3, which was fitted under GMACS 2.20.22 to a survey series ending in 2025, is not plotted."}

# --- 1. Process Prediction Data and Add Hybrid Status ---
dfrIndxFit_plot <- wtsGMACS::extractRep1Results(reslst, "Index_fit_summary") |> 
  dplyr::filter(case != "25.1 gmacs" & maturity != "immature") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    across(c(year, obs, base_CV, actual_CV, q, prd, prsn_res), as.numeric)
  ) |> 
  dplyr::rename(
    predicted = prd,
    residuals = prsn_res,
    model     = case
  ) |> 
  dplyr::mutate(
    # Categorize models based on the long label *before* shortening it
    hybrid_status = ifelse(grepl("hyb_surv|hyb_both", model, ignore.case = TRUE),
                           "Hybrid Included",
                           "Standard Survey"),
    maturity_status = ifelse(grepl("new_mat", model, ignore.case = TRUE),
                           "New maturity",
                           "Old maturity"),
    # Compact shortname for the legend
    model = to_short(model),
    # Confidence interval calculations
    sd_log = sqrt(log(1 + actual_CV^2)),
    lba    = qlnorm(0.05, log(obs), sd_log),
    uba    = qlnorm(0.95, log(obs), sd_log)
  )

check <- dfrIndxFit_plot %>%
  filter(year == 2019 & sex == "male") %>%
  select(sex, hybrid_status, maturity_status, obs, model)

# --- 2. Extract Unique Observations ---
# This ensures we only plot a single set of points and black error bars
dfrObs <- dfrIndxFit_plot |> 
  dplyr::distinct(year, sex, hybrid_status, maturity_status, obs, lba, uba)

# --- 3. Generate the 4-Panel Plot ---
p_idx_final <- ggplot() +
  # Model Predictions (Colored lines, plotted first so they sit behind points)
  geom_line(
    data = dfrIndxFit_plot, 
    aes(x = year, y = predicted, color = model), 
    lwd = 0.9, 
    alpha = 0.8
  ) +
  # Observations (Single black error bar per year/sex/panel)
  geom_errorbar(
    data = dfrObs,
    aes(x = year, ymin = lba, ymax = uba), 
    width = 0.3, 
    color = "black",
    alpha = 0.6
  ) +
  # Observations (Single black point per year/sex/panel)
  geom_point(
    data = dfrObs,
    aes(x = year, y = obs), 
    size = 1.2,
    color = "black"
  ) +
  # Formatting and Scales
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, NA), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))) +
  labs(
    x = "Year", 
    y = "NMFS Survey Biomass (1,000 t)",
    color = "Model Prediction",
    subtitle = "Points/Bars: Shared Observations | Lines: Model Fits",
    caption = "Error bars represent 95% log-normal confidence intervals on observations."
  ) +
  facet_grid(sex ~ hybrid_status + maturity_status, scales = "free_y") + 
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.text = element_text(size = 8),
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "white"),
    panel.spacing = unit(1, "lines")
  )

print(p_idx_final)

```{r catchfits, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=F, fig.width=8, fig.height=8, fig.cap="Model fits to catch data (1,000 t), for all models presented."}

# --- 1. Process Catch Fit Data and Add Hybrid Status ---
dfrCatFit_plot <- wtsGMACS::extractRep1Results(reslst, "Catch_fit_summary") |> 
  dplyr::mutate(
    # Ensure numeric types
    across(c(year, obs, cv, effort, HM, prd, rsd), as.numeric)
  ) |> 
  dplyr::rename(
    predicted = prd,
    residuals = rsd,
    model     = case
  ) |> 
  dplyr::mutate(

    hybrid_status = ifelse(grepl("hyb_both|hyb_fishery", model, ignore.case = TRUE),

                           "Standard Data"),
    # Compact shortname for the legend
    model = to_short(model),
    # Create descriptive row labels for faceting
    series = dplyr::case_when(
      fleet == "Trawl_Bycatch" ~ "Non-directed Bycatch",
      type == "retained" ~ "Directed Retained (Male)",
      type == "discard" & sex == "male"   ~ "Directed Discard (Male)",

    y = "Catch (1,000 t)",
    color = "Model Scenario",
    title = "Fishery Catch and Bycatch Fits",

    strip.text.y = element_text(size = 8, angle = 0), # Keep labels readable

```{r obs-101-vs-pred, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=F, out.width="100%", fig.width=6.5, fig.height=7, fig.cap="Estimated abundance of male crab >101mm carapace width from the survey (black line and dots with gray 95% CI) and from each model in the assessment (colored lines)."}
EBSdata	<-read.csv("data/survey/survey_large_male_index_derived.csv")
EBSdata	<-EBSdata[EBSdata$CATEGORY=="preferred_male",]
#==make upper and lower CIs
EBSdata$upper_bio_ci<-exp(log(EBSdata$BIOMASS_MT)+1.96*(sqrt(log(1+EBSdata$BIOMASS_MT_CV^2))))
EBSdata$lower_bio_ci<-exp(log(EBSdata$BIOMASS_MT)-1.96*(sqrt(log(1+EBSdata$BIOMASS_MT_CV^2))))
EBSdata$upper_abn_ci<-exp(log(EBSdata$ABUNDANCE)+1.96*(sqrt(log(1+EBSdata$ABUNDANCE_CV^2))))
EBSdata$lower_abn_ci<-exp(log(EBSdata$ABUNDANCE)-1.96*(sqrt(log(1+EBSdata$ABUNDANCE_CV^2))))

#==take predicted survey
dfrN_YXMSZ = wtsGMACS::extractRep1Results(reslst,"N_YXMSZ") |> 
  tidyr::pivot_longer(cols=!c(case,year,sex,maturity,shell_con),
                      names_to="size",
                      values_to="est") |> 
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(c(year,size,est),
                              as.numeric),
                xm=paste(maturity,sex)
  );

pred_101_n2<-filter(dfrN_YXMSZ,sex=='male'&size>101)%>%

pred_101_n2$tot_ABN<-(pred_101_n2$ABN+pred_101_n3$ABN)

# Shortnames for the color legend
pred_101_n2$case <- to_short(pred_101_n2$case)


male_101<-EBSdata
div_n<-1000
large_males2<-ggplot()+

```{r predfmort, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=F, fig.height=8, fig.width=8, fig.cap="Estimated fishing mortalities (per year) for the directed and non-directed fisheries."}

# --- 1. Robust Data Extraction across Models ---
# We loop through all models in reslst to find the correctly named F-dataframe
dfrF_plot <- names(reslst$repsLst) |> 
  purrr::map_dfr(function(c_name) {
    rep_obj <- reslst$repsLst[[c_name]]
    
    # Identify which name this specific model run used
    f_df_name <- intersect(
      names(rep_obj), 
      c("Fully-selected_capture_rate_by_season_sex_and_fishery", 
        "Fully-selected_FM_by_season_sex_and_fishery")
    )[1]
    
    if (is.na(f_df_name)) return(NULL)
    
    # Extract and clean
    rep_obj[[f_df_name]] |> 
      dplyr::mutate(
        Model = c_name,
        # Ensure consistency across versions (some use 'year', others 'Year')
        Year = as.numeric(year)
      )
  })

# --- 2. Clean and Filter Data for Plotting ---
plot_dat <- dfrF_plot |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    # Rename fleets for the report
    Fleet = dplyr::case_when(
      fleet == "Pot_Fishery" ~ "Directed Pot Fishery",
      fleet == "Trawl_Bycatch" ~ "Non-directed Bycatch",
      TRUE ~ fleet
    ),
    # Capitalize sex for headers
    Sex = stringr::str_to_title(sex),
    # Ensure mortality values are numeric (assuming season 2 is the primary fishery)
    F_value = as.numeric(`2`),
    # Compact shortname for the legend
    Model   = to_short(Model)
  ) |>
  # Filter only for the primary fishing fleets
  dplyr::filter(Fleet %in% c("Directed Pot Fishery", "Non-directed Bycatch"))

# --- 3. Generate the Comparison Plot ---
p_f_mort <- ggplot(plot_dat, aes(x = Year, y = F_value, color = Model, group = Model)) +
  # Model estimates
  geom_line(lwd = 1.1, alpha = 0.7) +
  # Layout and Scales
  facet_grid(Fleet ~ Sex, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, NA), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(
    title = "Estimated Fully-Selected Fishing Mortality",
    subtitle = "Calculated for the primary fishing season (Season 2)",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Fishing Mortality (F)",
    color = element_blank()
  ) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "white"),
    panel.spacing = unit(1, "lines")
  )

print(p_f_mort)

```

  purrr::map_dfr(function(case_name) {
    # Access the output list directly
    dat <- reslst$outsLst[[case_name]]$mature_probability
    
    if (is.null(dat)) {
      message("Warning: No mature_probability data for ", case_name)
      return(NULL)
    }
    
    # Pivot from wide to long format
    dat %>%
      tidyr::pivot_longer(
        cols = -c(Sex, Year),
        names_to = "width",
        values_to = "prob"
      ) %>%
      dplyr::mutate(
        # Compact shortname for the legend
        Model = as.character(to_short(case_name)),
        # Logic to separate models with "newmat" (uses long label for the test)
        Maturity_Source = ifelse(grepl("new_mat", case_name, ignore.case = TRUE),
                                 "New Maturity Workflow",
                                 "Standard Maturity Data"),
        width = as.numeric(as.character(width)),
        prob = as.numeric(prob),
        # Ensure Year is a factor for discrete coloring if desired,
        # or keep numeric for a gradient
        Year_Fact = as.factor(Year)
      )
  })

# --- 2. Generate the Split Plot ---
p_molt <- plotdat_all %>%
  mutate(Year = as.numeric(Year)) %>%
 ggplot(aes(x = width, y = prob, color = Year_Fact)) +
  # Use group to ensure lines are drawn per Year/Model combination
  geom_line(lwd = 1.1, alpha = 0.7) +
  # Force y-axis from 0 to 1
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(
    x = "Carapace Width (mm)", 
    y = "Probability of Terminal Molt",
    col = "Year",
    title = "Probability of Maturing / Terminal Molt",
    subtitle = "Separated by Maturity Data Specification"
  ) +
  # Facet rows by Data Source (Standard vs Newmat) and columns by Sex
  facet_grid(Maturity_Source ~ Sex) + 
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "white"),
    panel.spacing = unit(1, "lines")
  )

# Render the plot
print(p_molt)

# Size composition fits

```{r size-comp-plots, results='asis', echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, out.width="100%"}

# Order comp plots by base fleet, comp_type, sex, maturity so that fits across
# model variants (hybrid/compfix/plus_group; new vs. old maturity ogive) for
# the same data block sit next to each other.
img_folder <- "plots"
img_files  <- list.files(path = img_folder, pattern = "^size_comp_plot_", full.names = TRUE)

parse_meta <- function(f) {
  base  <- tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(f))
  desc  <- sub("^size_comp_plot_\\d+_", "", base)
  parts <- strsplit(desc, "_")[[1]]
  sex_idx <- which(parts %in% c("male", "female"))[1]
  if (is.na(sex_idx)) {
    return(data.frame(file = f, fleet_full = NA_character_, base_fleet = NA_character_,
                      comp_type = NA_character_, sex = NA_character_,
                      maturity = NA_character_, ogive = NA_character_,
                      stringsAsFactors = FALSE))
  }
  fleet_full <- paste(parts[seq_len(sex_idx - 1)], collapse = "_")
  sex        <- parts[sex_idx]
  comp_type  <- parts[sex_idx + 1]
  maturity   <- parts[sex_idx + 2]
  ogive      <- if (sex_idx + 3 <= length(parts))
                  paste(parts[seq(sex_idx + 3, length(parts))], collapse = "_") else NA_character_
  base_fleet <- tolower(fleet_full)
  base_fleet <- sub("_(hybrid|compfix|plus_group)$", "", base_fleet)
  data.frame(file = f, fleet_full = fleet_full, base_fleet = base_fleet,
             comp_type = comp_type, sex = sex, maturity = maturity, ogive = ogive,
             stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}

meta <- do.call(rbind, lapply(img_files, parse_meta))

meta$comp_type <- factor(meta$comp_type, levels = c("retained", "total", "discarded"))
meta$sex       <- factor(meta$sex,       levels = c("female", "male"))
meta$maturity  <- factor(meta$maturity,  levels = c("immature", "mature", "undetermined"))

meta <- meta[order(meta$base_fleet, meta$comp_type, meta$sex, meta$maturity,
                   meta$fleet_full, meta$ogive), ]

make_caption <- function(f) {
  base <- tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(f))
  desc <- sub("^size_comp_plot_\\d+_", "", base)
  desc <- gsub("_", " ", desc)
  # "compfix" and "plus group" are internal configuration shorthands from the
  # fleet-splitting in the setup chunk; they read as if they were separate
  # fleets. Name what they mean, and say which models are plotted -- the caption
  # previously identified the panel only by maturity workflow (2026-08-29).
  desc <- sub("Pot fishery compfix", "Pot Fishery (corrected composition)", desc)
  desc <- sub("Pot fishery plus group", "Pot Fishery (expanded plus group)", desc)
  desc <- sub("NMFS Trawl", "NMFS trawl survey", desc)
  paste0("Model fits (lines) to size composition data (grey bars), all models ",
         "presented: ", desc, ". Proportions by 5 mm carapace-width bin.")
}

# Initialize trackers with empty strings
last_fleet <- ""
last_sex_mat <- ""

for (i in 1:nrow(meta)) {
  row <- meta[i, ]
  
  # 1. Check for Fleet change (## Header)
  if (row$base_fleet != last_fleet) {
    # Print the header (cleaning up underscores for readability)
    cat("\n## Fleet: ", tools::toTitleCase(gsub("_", " ", row$base_fleet)), "\n\n")
    
    # Update tracker
    last_fleet <- row$base_fleet
    # Reset sex_mat tracker so it prints for the new fleet section 
    # even if it's the same category as the end of the last fleet
    last_sex_mat <- "" 
  }
  
  # 2. Check for Sex/Maturity change (### Header)
  current_sex_mat <- paste(row$sex, "and", row$maturity)
  if (current_sex_mat != last_sex_mat) {
    cat("\n### ", tools::toTitleCase(current_sex_mat), "\n\n")
    last_sex_mat <- current_sex_mat
  }
  
  # 3. Print the Plot
  # {width=100%} is required. These are raw markdown images emitted with cat(),
  # so the chunk's out.width does NOT apply to them -- knitr only sizes figures
  # it generates itself. The size-comp PNGs are 8 x 8 in at 300 dpi against a
  # 6.5 in text width, so without this they ran off the page (2026-08-29).
  cat("![", make_caption(row$file), "](", URLencode(row$file), "){width=100%}\n\n", sep = "")
  
  # Optional: Add page break after every plot, or move this inside the header 
  # logic if you only want page breaks between fleets.
  cat("\\newpage\n\n")
}


```

# Appendix B. Convergence diagnostics

```{r conv-appendix-setup, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
## Appendix C reads the PER-MODEL jitter files. 05_run_jitter.R writes
## Models/rda_jitter.RData at a fixed path whatever --model is given, so each run
## overwrites the last; the per-model copies below are what survives. Absent
## files drop out with a visible note rather than a plausible blank row.
##
## Only WITHIN-model statistics are tabulated -- how often a model finds its own
## best optimum. Likelihoods are NOT compared across these rows: two of the three
## experiments run on forked TPLs whose objective functions carry terms stock
## 2.20.34 does not have (see diagnostic_models in 0-models.R).
conv_files <- c(
  "Model 26.1b (accepted)" = "Models/rda_jitter.RData",
  "Model 26.2 (male-only)" = "Models/rda_jitter_male_only.RData",
  "Model 26.1c (2019 data)" = "Models/rda_jitter_data2019.RData",
  "Model 26.1 (2025 base)"  = "Models/rda_jitter_25.2c.RData",
  "26.d1 stability"         = "Models/rda_jitter_stability.RData",
  "26.d3 eqmdevs"           = "Models/rda_jitter_eqmdevs.RData",
  "26.d4 combined"          = "Models/rda_jitter_combined.RData",
  "26.d5 male-only+eqmdevs" = "Models/rda_jitter_male_only_eqmdevs.RData"
)

conv_row <- function(lab, path) {
  if (!file.exists(path)) return(NULL)
  e <- new.env(); load(path, envir = e); j <- e$jitter
  sm <- j$summary; rs <- j$results
  ok <- !is.na(rs$mode)                       # runs that reached an optimum
  ## The recovery rate that matters is for the model's OWN BEST fit, which is not
  ## what pct_at_best_mode reports. classify_modes() (R/gmacs_jitter.R:604) orders
  ## clusters by their MINIMUM nll and letters them A, B, C best-first, but only
  ## once a cluster holds >= 3 runs; smaller ones are bucketed "minor" whatever
  ## their likelihood. So mode A is the best LETTERED cluster, not the best
  ## solution found: when the true best fit is reached by one or two runs it is
  ## bucketed minor and A is a worse optimum entirely. That is the accepted
  ## model's case exactly. Computed directly here for every model.
  best <- min(rs$objFun[ok], na.rm = TRUE)
  n_at_best <- sum(abs(rs$objFun[ok] - best) < 0.01)
  nmodes <- length(setdiff(unique(rs$mode[ok]), "minor"))
  ## OFL spread across NEAR-OPTIMAL runs (within 2 nll of the best), not across
  ## all usable ones. The all-runs spread answers "how bad can a converged but
  ## wrong run be", which is not the question here and inverts the ranking: on
  ## all usable runs the male-only model looks the WORST of the four despite
  ## having by far the best recovery rate, because its poor runs are further
  ## away. Conditioning on near-optimal runs asks how much the OFL moves among
  ## solutions the data cannot separate, which is the management-relevant spread.
  near <- ok & (rs$objFun - best) <= 2
  n_near <- sum(near)
  ofl_sp <- if (n_near > 1)
    100 * (max(rs$ofl_tot[near]) - min(rs$ofl_tot[near])) / min(rs$ofl_tot[near]) else NA_real_
  data.frame(
    Model = lab,
    Converged = sprintf("%d/%d", sm$n_converged[1], sm$n_runs[1]),
    `Meets 1e-3` = sprintf("%d/%d", sm$n_meets_conventional[1], sm$n_runs[1]),
    Minima = nmodes,
    `Best fit found` = sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)", n_at_best, 100 * n_at_best / sum(ok)),
    `Best lettered mode` = sprintf("%.1f%%", sm$pct_at_best_mode[1]),
    `OFL spread, near-optimal` = if (is.na(ofl_sp)) sprintf("- (n=%d)", n_near)
                                 else sprintf("%.1f%% (n=%d)", ofl_sp, n_near),
    `nll span` = sprintf("%.1f", diff(range(rs$objFun[ok], na.rm = TRUE))),
    check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}

conv_tab <- do.call(rbind, Map(conv_row, names(conv_files), conv_files))

## Statistics quoted in the concluding paragraph. Computed, not written down:
## three of the review findings on this appendix were hardcoded literals that had
## gone stale against a re-promoted fit, and this paragraph is its most quoted.
.rate <- function(path) {
  if (!file.exists(path)) return(c(NA, NA))
  e <- new.env(); load(path, envir = e); rs <- e$jitter$results
  ok <- !is.na(rs$mode); best <- min(rs$objFun[ok], na.rm = TRUE)
  c(sum(abs(rs$objFun[ok] - best) < 0.01), sum(ok))
}
.r_acc <- .rate(conv_files[["Model 26.1b (accepted)"]])
## Recovery rates are reported as counts with a confidence interval. A formal
## test of proportions was drafted here and removed (Grant, 2026-08-30): the
## p-value is not the register this document is read in, and the interval makes
## the same point -- where two intervals overlap heavily, 100 runs cannot
## separate the configurations.
.ci <- function(path) {
  r <- .rate(path)
  if (anyNA(r)) return(c(NA_real_, NA_real_))
  100 * stats::binom.test(r[1], r[2])$conf.int[1:2]
}
cv_pct_acc  <- 100 * .r_acc[1] / .r_acc[2]
cv_ci_hi    <- 100 * stats::binom.test(.r_acc[1], .r_acc[2])$conf.int[2]
cv_n_acc    <- .r_acc[2]
.r_eqm  <- .rate(conv_files[["26.d3 eqmdevs"]])
.r_stab <- .rate(conv_files[["26.d1 stability"]])
.r_mo   <- .rate(conv_files[["Model 26.2 (male-only)"]])
cv_pct_eqm  <- 100 * .r_eqm[1] / .r_eqm[2]
cv_pct_stab <- 100 * .r_stab[1] / .r_stab[2]
cv_pct_mo   <- 100 * .r_mo[1] / .r_mo[2]
## 26.d5 is the one configuration that improved on the model it was built from,
## so it is tested against 26.2 rather than against the accepted two-sex model.
.r_d5 <- .rate(conv_files[["26.d5 male-only+eqmdevs"]])
.r_d4 <- .rate(conv_files[["26.d4 combined"]])
cv_pct_d5  <- 100 * .r_d5[1] / .r_d5[2]
cv_pct_d4  <- 100 * .r_d4[1] / .r_d4[2]
cv_ci_d5   <- .ci(conv_files[["26.d5 male-only+eqmdevs"]])
cv_ci_mo   <- .ci(conv_files[["Model 26.2 (male-only)"]])
cv_ci_stab <- .ci(conv_files[["26.d1 stability"]])
cv_ci_eqm  <- .ci(conv_files[["26.d3 eqmdevs"]])

## Where the movement between optima actually sits, by parameter class. Written
## by 05b_jitter_movement_decomposition.R; movement is the RANGE (max - min) of
## each parameter across the retained optima, summed within class. Range rather
## than variance because these are alternative optima, not draws from a
## distribution -- one run at an extreme is as meaningful as the spread of the
## rest. Retained = converged (max|grad| < 1e-2) AND within 2 nll of the best,
## which is what keeps this a measure of the likelihood's shape near the optimum
## rather than a measure of optimiser failure.
mv_all <- Sys.glob("data/diagnostics/jitter_movement_by_class_*.csv")
## Pick the ACCEPTED model's file by name. A sort order would select it only by
## alphabetical accident and would silently switch models when another
## configuration is decomposed.
mv_path <- grep("26_gmacs_update_newmat_plus_group", mv_all, value = TRUE)
mv_have <- length(mv_path) == 1
if (mv_have) {
  mv <- read.csv(mv_path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  mv <- mv[order(-mv$share_pct), ]
  ## Shares are recomputed from total_range rather than read, so a hand-edited
  ## share_pct column cannot reach the page.
  mv$share_pct <- 100 * mv$total_range / sum(mv$total_range)
  stopifnot("movement shares must sum to 100" = abs(sum(mv$share_pct) - 100) < 1e-6)
  .sh <- function(cl) sum(mv$share_pct[mv$class %in% cl])
  mv_sexalloc <- .sh("sex allocation")
  mv_female   <- .sh(c("female", "female (F offsets)"))
  mv_male     <- .sh("male")
  mv_fem_plus <- mv_sexalloc + mv_female
  mv_n_opt    <- mv$n_optima[1]
  mv_npar_m   <- mv$n_parameters[mv$class == "male"]
  mv_npar_sa  <- mv$n_parameters[mv$class == "sex allocation"]
  ## Movement PER PARAMETER. The raw counts invite a misleading comparison --
  ## "female" is split across two classes, so male (101) exceeds the female class
  ## (91) but not the female classes combined (134). Density avoids the question
  ## and is the sharper statement anyway.
  .dens <- function(cl) sum(mv$total_range[mv$class %in% cl]) / sum(mv$n_parameters[mv$class %in% cl])
  mv_dens_sa   <- .dens("sex allocation")
  mv_dens_male <- .dens("male")
  mv_dens_ratio <- mv_dens_sa / mv_dens_male
} else {
  mv_sexalloc <- mv_female <- mv_male <- mv_fem_plus <- NA_real_
  mv_dens_sa <- mv_dens_male <- mv_dens_ratio <- NA_real_
  mv_npar_m <- mv_npar_sa <- mv_n_opt <- NA_integer_
}

## Cross-model comparison. Shares are the safe currency here: movement is a RANGE
## across retained optima, and range is not independent of how many optima were
## retained (40 / 20 / 31 across these models), so absolute totals carry a caveat
## that shares do not. `26.d1 stability` is absent by necessity, not oversight --
## only 2 of its runs land within 2 nll of its best fit, below the 3 the
## decomposition needs, because its optima are too dispersed to form a cluster.
.mv_lab <- c("26_gmacs_update_newmat_plus_group" = "Model 26.1b (accepted)",
             "26_gmacs_eqmdevs"                  = "26.d3 eqmdevs",
             "26_gmacs_male_only"                = "Model 26.2 (male-only)",
             "26_gmacs_male_only_eqmdevs"        = "26.d5 male-only + eqmdevs")
## Restrict to the configurations this appendix actually discusses. Decomposition
## files for other models appear in data/diagnostics/ as the diagnostic work
## continues; a new one must not silently join the table (nor abort the knit, as
## it did on 2026-08-30 when a male_only_eqmdevs file landed mid-session). An
## unrecognised file is reported in the console and skipped.
.mv_known <- Filter(function(f) {
  m <- read.csv(f, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)$model[1]
  ok <- m %in% names(.mv_lab)
  if (!ok) message("conv-appendix: skipping unlisted decomposition for '", m, "'")
  ok
}, mv_all)
xm_have <- length(.mv_known) > 1
if (xm_have) {
  xm <- do.call(rbind, lapply(.mv_known, function(f) {
    d <- read.csv(f, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    tot <- sum(d$total_range)
    cls <- function(cl) sum(d$total_range[d$class %in% cl])
    data.frame(
      Model = unname(.mv_lab[d$model[1]]),
      Minima = d$n_optima[1],
      `Total movement` = tot,
      `Sex allocation (%)` = 100 * cls("sex allocation") / tot,
      `Female + sex allocation (%)` = 100 * cls(c("female", "female (F offsets)", "sex allocation")) / tot,
      `Male (%)` = 100 * cls("male") / tot,
      `Male movement` = cls("male"),
      check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  }))
  xm <- xm[order(-xm$`Total movement`), ]
  stopifnot("a cross-model row lost its label" = !any(is.na(xm$Model)))
  ## Plain-named scalars for the prose. Inline `r ` code cannot carry
  ## backtick-quoted column names, so pull them out here.
  .xg <- function(col, mdl) xm[[col]][xm$Model == mdl]
  xm_male_acc  <- .xg("Male movement", "Model 26.1b (accepted)")
  xm_male_eqm  <- .xg("Male movement", "26.d3 eqmdevs")
  xm_male_pct_eqm <- .xg("Male (%)", "26.d3 eqmdevs")
  xm_sa_eqm    <- .xg("Sex allocation (%)", "26.d3 eqmdevs")
  xm_fp_eqm    <- .xg("Female + sex allocation (%)", "26.d3 eqmdevs")
  xm_tot_acc   <- .xg("Total movement", "Model 26.1b (accepted)")
  xm_tot_male  <- .xg("Total movement", "Model 26.2 (male-only)")
  xm_optima_lab <- paste(xm$Minima, collapse = ", ")   # table row order, not sorted
} else {
  xm_male_acc <- xm_male_eqm <- xm_sa_eqm <- xm_fp_eqm <- NA_real_
  xm_tot_acc <- xm_tot_male <- NA_real_; xm_optima_lab <- "NA"
}
conv_have <- !is.null(conv_tab) && nrow(conv_tab) > 0
if (conv_have) stopifnot(
  "a convergence row lost its model label" = !any(is.na(conv_tab$Model)))
```

\newpage

The June 2026 SSC asked that a focused convergence section identify which parameters separate the jitter minima. This appendix collects the jitter evidence for every model jittered this cycle, together with four structural experiments built specifically to diagnose the multimodality: `26.d1 stability`, `26.d3 eqmdevs`, `26.d4 combined`, and `26.d5`, the male-only model with the equilibrium-backbone initialization. A fifth, `26.d2 initscaled`, was set aside without jittering. None of the experiments is an assessment model and none is proposed for any purpose other than diagnosis. They are registered separately from the model set in `0-models.R` for that reason.

The diagnostic identified three independent pathologies in the accepted model:

1. `M_pars_est[15]`, the 2019 immature-female natural mortality deviation, is structurally non-identified. It is the only one of the 412 parameters that moves while the objective function does not.
2. The recruitment sex ratio is controlled by 44 logit parameters bounded at plus or minus 100, whose only effective restraint is a penalty standard deviation of 2.0 hardcoded in the source rather than read from the control file. Thirteen of the 44 are estimated beyond two standard deviations of that penalty. They are nowhere near the plus or minus 100 bounds (the estimates span -3.6 to +4.2), so it is the penalty, not the bound, that is failing to restrain them.
3. The 1982 initial numbers at length are 83 parameters whose overall level is entirely unpenalized. The only term touching them is a first-difference smoothness penalty, and first differences are invariant to shifting a whole group.

The attribution analysis identifies the same parameters. Among the parameters that most separate the jitter minima (Table \@ref(tab:jitter-attribution)), the largest is `logit_rec_prop_est`, the recruitment sex allocation. The second pathology above is therefore the leading determinant of which minimum a run reaches. This addresses the SSC's request, and it is consistent with the male-only simplification, which removes the sex allocation entirely, being the only configuration in Table \@ref(tab:conv-table) that reliably recovers its own best fit.

Decomposing the movement between minima by parameter class quantifies this (Table \@ref(tab:movement-table)). Across the `r mv_n_opt` near-equivalent minima, the recruitment sex allocation alone accounts for `r .f(mv_sexalloc, 1)` percent of all parameter movement, and the female and sex-allocation parameters together account for `r .f(mv_fem_plus, 1)` percent. The male parameters account for `r .f(mv_male, 1)` percent across `r mv_npar_m` parameters, whereas the sex allocation reaches `r .f(mv_sexalloc, 1)` percent on just `r mv_npar_sa` parameters, about `r .f(mv_dens_ratio, 0)` times as much movement per parameter. The alternative minima are therefore largely disagreements about the female population and the split of recruitment between the sexes, rather than about the male population the assessment exists to manage. This is the clearest quantitative case for the male-only direction, and it is measured on the accepted model itself rather than inferred from the sensitivity.

Running the same decomposition on the structural experiments explains these results (Table \@ref(tab:xmodel-table)). The equilibrium backbone in `26.d3 eqmdevs` had its intended effect and no other: the male parameters' share of movement fell from `r .f(mv_male, 1)` to `r .f(xm_male_pct_eqm, 1)` percent, because anchoring the 1982 structure removes the freedom that had been propagating through the male side. It does not affect the sex ratio, and sex-allocation movement barely changed, so its share rose from `r .f(mv_sexalloc, 1)` to `r .f(xm_sa_eqm, 1)` percent and the female-and-sex-allocation total from `r .f(mv_fem_plus, 1)` to `r .f(xm_fp_eqm, 1)` percent. Fixing the initialization made the sex allocation more dominant, not less, which explains why it did not improve the recovery rate.

`Model 26.2` removes the sex allocation altogether, and total movement falls from `r .f(xm_tot_acc, 1)` to `r .f(xm_tot_male, 2)`, with the remainder dominated by the shared recruitment deviations. The parameters `Model 26.2` removes are the ones responsible for almost all of the movement between minima, which is the source of its advantage rather than the parameter count itself. Two qualifications apply. The absolute movement totals are ranges taken across different numbers of retained minima (`r xm_optima_lab` across the models shown), and a range depends on how many runs enter it, so the totals should be read as indicative while the shares, which are unaffected, are the basis for the comparison. `26.d1 stability` cannot appear in this table because only two of its runs land within two likelihood units of its best fit, fewer than the decomposition requires. Its minima are too dispersed to form a cluster of near-equivalent solutions, consistent with its likelihood span being among the widest in Table \@ref(tab:conv-table) (311.8 compared with the accepted model's 301.6).

Each experiment addressed a different subset of the pathologies. `26.d1 stability` fixed the first two and left the third. `26.d3 eqmdevs` replaced the third with an equilibrium backbone times penalized deviations and left the first two. `26.d2 initscaled` rescaled the initial-condition parameterization and was set aside without jittering when its fit to the data proved 138 likelihood units worse. A configuration with all three fixed at once, `26.d4`, was then built and jittered, and it did not resolve the multimodality either. What did work was applying the equilibrium-backbone initialization to the male-only model rather than to the two-sex one.

The pattern across the table is that the two-sex reconfigurations did not work and the male-only one did. The accepted model recovers its own best fit in `r .f(cv_pct_acc, 1)` percent of converged runs and `26.d3 eqmdevs` in `r .f(cv_pct_eqm, 1)` percent. Those differences, and `26.d1 stability`'s `r .f(cv_pct_stab, 1)` percent, are too small to be resolved by 100 runs. The 95 percent confidence interval on the accepted model's `r .f(.r_acc[1], 0)`-in-`r cv_n_acc` rate runs from zero to about `r .f(cv_ci_hi, 0)` percent, and the intervals for `eqmdevs` (to `r .f(cv_ci_eqm[2], 0)` percent) and `stability` (to `r .f(cv_ci_stab[2], 0)` percent) sit almost entirely inside it. Separating rates of this size would take several hundred runs. None of these experiments improved recovery detectably. The apparent declines are within what 100 runs can resolve. `26.d4 combined`, which applies all three fixes at once, is no better: `r .f(cv_pct_d4, 1)` percent, well inside the range the accepted model's own rate could take, and it converged less often than any other configuration. Its printed "best mode" share of 16.7 percent must not be quoted as a recovery rate. That mode sits 5.9 likelihood units above its own best fit, which only `r .f(.r_d4[1], 0)` of `r .f(.r_d4[2], 0)` converged runs reached. Fixing all three pathologies in the two-sex model therefore does not resolve the multimodality.

Two configurations perform better than the rest, and both remove the female population. `Model 26.2` recovers its best fit in `r .f(cv_pct_mo, 1)` percent of converged runs (`r .f(.r_mo[1], 0)` of `r .f(.r_mo[2], 0)`). The accepted model recovers its own in one of `r cv_n_acc`. That gap is far larger than 100 runs could produce by chance. `26.d5`, which adds the equilibrium-backbone initialization to the male-only model, reaches `r .f(cv_pct_d5, 1)` percent (`r .f(.r_d5[1], 0)` of `r .f(.r_d5[2], 0)` runs), the only configuration tested that improved on the model it was derived from. Its likelihood span across usable runs is `r .f(diff(range(local({e<-new.env(); load(conv_files[["26.d5 male-only+eqmdevs"]], envir=e); r<-e$jitter$results; r$objFun[!is.na(r$mode)]}))), 1)` units, whereas every other configuration in the table spans more than a hundred, and its promoted fit is the only one in this study to meet the 0.001 gradient criterion. Two qualifications apply. The 95 percent confidence intervals on the two recovery rates overlap (`r .f(cv_ci_d5[1], 0)` to `r .f(cv_ci_d5[2], 0)` percent against `r .f(cv_ci_mo[1], 0)` to `r .f(cv_ci_mo[2], 0)`), so the improvement is real on this evidence but not decisive, and it rests on a single set of 100 runs. It also met the gradient criterion in only 3 runs of 100 against `Model 26.2`'s 9, so the two convergence measures disagree and both are reported. The recovery measure concerns which minimum a run finds, the gradient measure how precisely it stops.

The two changes are complementary. Removing the sex allocation removes the largest share of the movement between minima, and anchoring the initial condition removes most of what remains. Neither is enough on its own: the same initialization applied to the two-sex model, `26.d3`, changed nothing detectable. `eqmdevs` did halve the likelihood span across runs and roughly halve the penalty burden, which are real improvements in conditioning, but they did not translate into finding one minimum reliably. The male-only simplification is the configuration that materially improves recovery, at `r .f(cv_pct_mo, 1)` percent, and it is one of only two rows in the table where the best fit and the best lettered mode are the same solution (`Model 26.1`, the 2025 base, is the other). In the accepted model they are different solutions 0.81 likelihood units apart, and in `26.d3 eqmdevs` they also differ. In those configurations a single run from default starting values is more likely to reach a reproducible but inferior minimum than the best one. For this reason the male-only configuration is in the model set as `Model 26.2` and the structural experiments are not.

## Caveats

Three qualifications apply to the experiments above.

**The equilibrium backbone is unfished.** `26.d3 eqmdevs` anchors the 1982 population on an unfished equilibrium, following the formulation it was ported from, but the eastern Bering Sea snow crab stock had been fished since the late 1970s. The effect is visible in the result: 1982 mature male biomass moves from 212.9 to 300.9 kt. Switching the backbone to a fished equilibrium is a small change to the same code, and it has not been made, so this experiment should not be judged finally on the results reported here.

**Several of the experiments require modified source code.** `26.d1 stability`, `26.d3 eqmdevs`, `26.d4 combined` and `26.d5` were run with forked GMACS source trees rather than the stock 2.20.34 binary used for every model in the assessment. This matters most for `26.d5`, the configuration these results point toward: it cannot be reproduced, or brought forward as a candidate, until the initialization mode is merged into the released version. `stability` changes a penalty standard deviation that is hardcoded in the source rather than read from the control file. `eqmdevs` adds an initialization mode and a deviation penalty occupying a control-file slot that is dead code in the released version. The results in this appendix are therefore not reproducible with the stock binary, and the forks are recorded with the models. The shared source tree the assessment itself is built from is unmodified and is checked against its hash at every build.

**One of the fixes is a structural assumption, not a neutral correction.** Fixing the 2019 immature-female mortality deviation removes that mortality event for immature females entirely, while immature males and mature females retain theirs. This is defensible, because the data do not identify the parameter and estimating it is no more informative, but it is an assumption about what happened in 2019 and any configuration using it should be described that way. It is not, however, the main reason the experiments move the OFL. Isolating the changes shows the equilibrium initialization contributing more on its own than the mortality and sex-ratio fixes together, and `26.d3 eqmdevs` uses that initialization without the mortality fix at all. The OFL movement in these experiments should be attributed to the initialization first.
